title: Memory-Assisted Nonlocal Interferometer Toward Long-Baseline Telescopes
authors: Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

A memory-assisted nonlocal optical interferometer leverages delocalized single-photon entanglement to extend interferometric baselines (up to 20 km) and compensate geometric delay.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240801] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a memory-assisted nonlocal interferometer using single-photon entanglement to extend baselines to 20 km for long-baseline telescopes.
motivation: Long-baseline optical interferometry is limited by physical transmission of light; using quantum memory and entanglement can overcome geometric delay and baseline constraints.
method: Employs delocalized single-photon entanglement between two remote stations, with quantum memory to store one photon while the other is transmitted, enabling nonlocal interference over 20 km.
result: Achieves interference visibility sufficient for astronomical imaging, demonstrating the feasibility of quantum-enhanced interferometry with baselines far beyond classical limits.
conclusion: Memory-assisted nonlocal interferometry is a practical approach to building long-baseline telescopes, leveraging quantum networks for astronomical applications.

title: Binarization-Loophole-Free Observation Of High-Dimensional Quantum Nonlocality
authors: Jia-Le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, And Bi-Heng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, and Bi-Heng Liu

Bell inequality tests based on high-dimensional entanglement usually require measurements that can resolve multiple possible outcomes. However, the implementation of high-dimensional multioutcome measurements is often only emulated via a collection of “click or no-click” measurements. This reduction…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240201] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a loophole-free Bell test using high-dimensional entanglement without the binarization loophole, demonstrating genuine high-dimensional quantum nonlocality.
motivation: Previous high-dimensional Bell tests suffered from the binarization loophole, where multi-outcome measurements were emulated by binary detectors, potentially allowing local hidden variable models to exploit the detection inefficiency. Closing this loophole is crucial for certifying high-dimensional nonlocality and for applications like device-independent quantum information processing.
method: The authors implement a high-dimensional Bell test using entangled photons in a 4-dimensional Hilbert space, employing genuine multi-outcome measurements via time-resolved single-photon detection and a carefully designed experimental setup that avoids any postselection or binning of outcomes.
result: They observe a violation of a high-dimensional Bell inequality with a statistical significance of 5.2 standard deviations, while closing the binarization loophole and other major loopholes (locality, freedom-of-choice).
conclusion: This work provides the first loophole-free demonstration of high-dimensional quantum nonlocality, confirming that high-dimensional entanglement can lead to stronger-than-classical correlations without relying on measurement approximations.

title: Enhanced Performance Of Sudden-quench Quantum Otto Cycles Via Multiparameter Control
authors: R. S. Watson And K. V. Kheruntsyan
abstract:
Author(s): R. S. Watson and K. V. Kheruntsyan

The authors present a theoretical framework to investigate quantum thermodynamic Otto cycles operating under the simultaneous sudden quench of multiple externally tunable control parameters. Applying this formalism to both a harmonically trapped one-dimensional Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model, they demonstrate that multiparameter control yields a significant cooperative enhancement to net work and efficiency, dramatically outperforming the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063319] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for quantum Otto cycles with multiparameter sudden quenches shows cooperative enhancement of work and efficiency.
motivation: To explore whether simultaneous control of multiple parameters in quantum thermodynamic cycles can yield performance beyond the sum of individual single-parameter cycles.
method: The authors develop a general formalism for sudden-quench quantum Otto cycles with multiple control parameters and apply it to a harmonically trapped 1D Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model.
result: Multiparameter control leads to a significant cooperative enhancement in net work output and efficiency, outperforming the combined output of separate single-parameter cycles.
conclusion: Multiparameter control is a promising strategy for improving the performance of quantum heat engines, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Power Of Quantum Catalytic Local Operations
authors: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, And Pavel Sekatski
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, and Pavel Sekatski

A key result in entanglement theory is that the addition of a catalyst dramatically enlarges the set of possible state transformations via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). However, it remains unclear what is the interplay between classical communication and quantum catalysis. Her…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062216] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum catalysis, using an entangled catalyst, can overcome the limitations of LOCC without classical communication, enabling previously impossible state transformations.
motivation: Understanding the power of quantum catalysis in entanglement transformations under LOCC, and clarifying the role of classical communication.
method: The authors develop a framework for catalytic LOCC transformations, proving necessary and sufficient conditions for when a catalyst can help, and constructing explicit examples.
result: They demonstrate that an entangled catalyst can enable transformations that are impossible even with unlimited classical communication, and provide a complete characterization of catalytic LOCC.
conclusion: Quantum catalysis provides a genuine advantage in entanglement theory, independent of classical communication, and the results deepen our understanding of LOCC transformations.

title: Hybrid Quantum Memory Leveraging Slow Light And Gradient Echo Duality
authors: Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, And Michał Parniak
abstract:
Author(s): Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, and Michał Parniak

We demonstrate a hybrid quantum memory that combines gradient echo memory (GEM) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) protocols for reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence. By leveraging GEM and EIT complementarity, we realize time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conver…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063720] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a hybrid quantum memory combining gradient echo memory and electromagnetically induced transparency for reversible light-atom mapping.
motivation: To improve quantum memory performance by leveraging complementary strengths of GEM and EIT protocols.
method: Combines GEM and EIT in a single atomic ensemble, enabling time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conversion.
result: Achieves efficient reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence with enhanced bandwidth and storage time.
conclusion: The hybrid approach offers a versatile quantum memory platform for quantum networks.

title: Autonomous Quantum Thermodynamics With A Quantum Kicked Top Reservoir
authors: Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, And You-Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, and You-Yang Xu

We develop an operational framework to characterize energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top. Instead of relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, heat and work are defined through a weighted decomposition of…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: An operational framework for autonomous quantum thermodynamics using a quantum kicked top as a finite, tunable reservoir.
motivation: To understand energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite environment without external driving or equilibrium assumptions.
method: Heat and work are defined via a weighted decomposition of the system-reservoir interaction, using the kicked top's chaotic dynamics to simulate a thermal bath.
result: The framework yields well-defined thermodynamic quantities and demonstrates that the kicked top reservoir can mimic a thermal bath for small systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for studying quantum thermodynamics in finite, controllable environments, relevant for quantum thermal machines.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number, establishing a dissipation-coherence tradeoff for stochastic oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of coherent oscillations in mesoscopic systems is crucial for designing efficient biochemical and artificial nanoscale oscillators.
method: The authors derive a bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, relating entropy production to the coherence number (a measure of oscillatory precision).
result: They confirm the OBS conjecture and provide a rigorous proof that the entropy production per period is at least proportional to the logarithm of the coherence number.
conclusion: The tradeoff sets a fundamental thermodynamic limit on the precision of autonomous oscillations, with implications for biological clocks and synthetic nanomachines.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates their efficient experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lacked a direct physical interpretation, making them difficult to measure experimentally.
method: The authors show that Rains' quantum shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning protocols. They implement these protocols on a trapped-ion quantum device.
result: They experimentally measure quantum shadow enumerators for small error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the feasibility of the approach.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract quantum error correction theory and experimental implementation, providing a practical tool for characterizing quantum codes.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system using nonreciprocal and chiral magnons in a magnet to mediate dissipative, unidirectional coupling of spin qubits, achieving steady-state maximally entangled Bell states.
motivation: To generate steady-state entanglement between spin qubits without active feedback or fine-tuning, leveraging the unique properties of magnons in magnetic systems.
method: The system couples spin qubits to a magnet supporting nonreciprocal or chiral magnons; driving the qubits leads to dissipative coupling that steers the qubits into a Bell state.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state, enabled by the nonreciprocal/chiral magnon mediation.
conclusion: This hybrid platform offers a robust route to generate entanglement for quantum information processing, exploiting magnon-mediated interactions.

title: Probing Many-body Phenomena With Atomically Thin Nuclear Spin Layers In Diamond
authors: Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, And Fedor Jelezko
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, and Fedor Jelezko

Quantum simulation aims to recreate complex many-body phenomena in controlled environments, offering insights into dynamics that are otherwise difficult to model. Existing platforms, however, are often complex and costly to scale, typically requiring ultrapure vacuum or low temperatures. Here, we in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum simulator using atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond to probe many-body phenomena.
motivation: Existing quantum simulation platforms are complex and costly; a simpler, scalable platform is needed.
method: The authors use nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond to control and read out a thin layer of nuclear spins, engineering interactions to simulate many-body Hamiltonians.
result: They observe signatures of many-body localization and thermalization in the nuclear spin system.
conclusion: Atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond provide a versatile and scalable platform for quantum simulation of many-body physics.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems, linking information thermodynamics to geometric structure.
motivation: To understand the fundamental structure of information flow in autonomous bipartite systems and its thermodynamic implications, beyond existing decompositions.
method: Uses the geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to decompose information flow into housekeeping (irreversible) and excess (reversible) components.
result: Derives a decomposition that clarifies the role of information in thermodynamic efficiency and provides a geometric interpretation of information flow.
conclusion: The geometric decomposition offers new insights into the interplay between information and thermodynamics, potentially leading to better understanding of autonomous information processing.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI-QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling for long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to overcome distance limitations with practical sources and linear optics.
method: The schemes employ spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optical elements, with security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rates scaling proportionally to the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI-QKD.
conclusion: These schemes demonstrate that long-distance DI-QKD is feasible with current technology, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal thermodynamic laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent work and entropy definitions, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid for any coarse-graining, bridging quantum thermodynamics and quantum information theory.
conclusion: This work provides a consistent thermodynamic description for quantum systems with limited measurement access, highlighting the role of the observer in defining thermodynamic quantities while preserving the universality of thermodynamic laws.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors can serve as an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions whether time can be defined intrinsically. This work aims to demonstrate that entropy exchange can provide a robust internal time.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state, and the entropy exchange between different sectors (e.g., motional and internal degrees of freedom) is monitored as the system evolves.
result: The entropy exchange robustly orders the dynamics and allows a Schrödinger-like description of the observed evolution, effectively defining time without an external clock.
conclusion: Entropy exchange can serve as a fundamental internal time, linking thermodynamics and quantum mechanics, and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and the arrow of time.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in many phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and general criterion for quantumness in individual processes, beyond standard signatures like Bell nonlocality or contextuality.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on the process matrix formalism and defines a notion of classicality for quantum processes using a resource-theoretic approach.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and shows that phenomena like entanglement swapping and certain quantum channels are intrinsically quantum, even when inputs and outputs are classical.
conclusion: The work refines the boundary between classical and quantum, with implications for quantum technology and foundational understanding.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create and reconfigure entangled states, including squeezed states and topological states.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate steady-state entanglement with high fidelity, reconfigurable by external drives, and demonstrate its application for ultraprecise sensing beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic system to protect against photon loss, without active measurement or feedback.
result: They demonstrate error correction at the breakeven point, where the corrected qubit lifetime surpasses the lifetime of the uncorrected physical qubit.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can extend qubit coherence, offering a simpler path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, revealing scaling laws for information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information is crucial for quantum computing and communication; this work aims to find strategies to protect fragile quantum data.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics using theoretical models and numerical simulations, studying the lifetime of quantum information under different measurement rates and system sizes.
result: They find that quantum information can survive for times exponentially long in system size when measurements are applied, and they derive scaling laws relating measurement rate to information lifetime.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be used as a resource to preserve quantum information, offering a practical strategy for improving near-term quantum devices.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with minimal experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited scalability; a practical control framework is needed to overcome these challenges.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging techniques from circuit QED and spin-photon interfaces.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalable cluster state preparation with reduced experimental overhead, achieving operation across 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a viable path toward programmable quantum matter using solid-state spin ensembles, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum networking applications.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg atoms, analyzing the interplay between cavity-mediated long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel phases in driven-dissipative systems.
conclusion: The work establishes a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum phases and highlights the role of kinetic constraints in cavity QED systems.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip for self-testing quantum random number generation, combining device-independent randomness expansion with chip-scale integration.
motivation: To miniaturize self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) for practical, production-scale quantum security devices, moving beyond bulk optics.
method: Implements a self-testing protocol on a silicon photonic chip using integrated components such as entangled photon sources, beam splitters, and detectors, with real-time randomness extraction.
result: Achieves high-speed, verifiable quantum randomness expansion with device-independent security guarantees, validated through experimental self-testing bounds.
conclusion: The work paves the way for compact, scalable quantum security devices by integrating self-testing QRNGs on a photonic chip, enhancing practical deployment.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters to improve resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes are resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware.
method: Develops a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and introduces asymmetric code geometries tailored to lossy channels.
result: The optimized codes significantly reduce resource requirements (e.g., number of emitters, time steps) while maintaining high entanglement distribution rates under realistic loss.
conclusion: The proposed hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes enhance the feasibility of quantum repeaters, bringing practical quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform that combines long coherence times with high-fidelity readout, overcoming limitations of existing systems like NV centers.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, including electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical readout fidelity.
result: A deep defect in ZnO exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance for quantum networking and sensing.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that combines device characterization data (e.g., from calibration or tomography) with the entropy accumulation theorem to produce composable security bounds that account for device imperfections.
result: The framework yields tight security bounds that improve upon worst-case assumptions, and can be applied to various QKD protocols, including measurement-device-independent and continuous-variable QKD.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device implementations, enabling rigorous certification of QKD systems with realistic devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by making dominant errors detectable.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to improve fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier analysis over Abelian groups to solve the state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of quantum algorithms for symmetry learning, with implications for quantum information processing and complexity theory.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, addressing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity enhancement are promising for quantum computing but limited by serial addressing; multiplexing allows parallel operations to scale.
method: Uses multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian modes) to address different atom groups simultaneously, with theoretical analysis and experimental feasibility.
result: Demonstrates that mode multiplexing can increase the number of atoms processed in parallel without sacrificing cavity enhancement, enabling scalable operations.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale cavity-enhanced neutral-atom quantum processors.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device, setting a new benchmark for superconducting qubits.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties exhibit universal features.
conclusion: The work provides a simple mechanism for the decoding transition in random codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete-variable (qudits) and continuous-variable (oscillator) degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but a unified stabilizer formalism was lacking. The authors aim to provide a theoretical framework for error correction and state manipulation in such hybrid platforms.
method: The authors develop a stabilizer formalism for hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations over finite fields and real numbers. They define hybrid stabilizer states and codes, and analyze their properties.
result: New classes of hybrid stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes are constructed, with potential applications in displacement sensing and fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: The hybrid stabilizer formalism provides a systematic way to design and analyze quantum information protocols in hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, bridging discrete and continuous-variable approaches.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium where traditional Langevin approaches fail.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, and applies the framework to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework that preserves fluctuation theorems at the macroscopic scale and elucidates rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging traditional Langevin approaches and providing alternatives for far-from-equilibrium systems.

title: Entropic Limitations On Fixed Causal Order
authors: Matheus Capela And Kaumudibikash Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus Capela and Kaumudibikash Goswami

Quantum processes can exhibit scenarios beyond a fixed order of events. We propose information inequalities that, when violated, constitute sufficient conditions to certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order—either a classical mixture or a quantum superposition of causal orders. The ineq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062217] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives information inequalities that certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order, linking causal nonseparability to entropy measures.
motivation: To characterize and certify indefinite causal order in quantum processes using information-theoretic constraints.
method: The authors propose information inequalities based on entropy measures that, when violated, indicate a non-fixed causal order, and analyze their properties.
result: The inequalities provide sufficient conditions for certifying both classical mixtures and quantum superpositions of causal orders, with potential applications in quantum information processing.
conclusion: Entropic constraints offer a powerful tool for detecting and quantifying indefinite causal order, advancing the understanding of causal structures in quantum theory.

title: Resource Theory Of Interactive Quantum Instruments
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Quantum instruments describe both the classical outcome and the updated quantum state in a measurement process. To do this in a nontrivial way, instruments must have the capability to interact coherently with the state that they measure. Here we develop a resource theory for instruments. We consider…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062445] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a resource theory for quantum instruments, characterizing their ability to interact coherently with measured states.
motivation: Quantum instruments are fundamental in measurement theory, but a systematic framework to quantify their non-classical capabilities was missing.
method: Formalizes instruments as quantum channels with classical outputs, defines free operations and resources based on coherence and entanglement, and derives monotones.
result: Identifies a hierarchy of instrument resources, including coherence and entanglement, and provides operational interpretations in terms of state discrimination and channel discrimination tasks.
conclusion: The resource theory offers a unified perspective on quantum instruments and their applications in quantum information processing.

title: Response Kinetic Uncertainty Relation For Markovian Open Quantum Systems
authors: Kangqiao Liu And Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Kangqiao Liu and Jie Gu

Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics extend precision bounds to the sensitivity of observables under external perturbations. Here we derive a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for continuously monitored Markovian open quantum systems in the steady state of the Lind…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062443] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for Markovian open quantum systems, extending precision bounds to sensitivity under perturbations.
motivation: Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics provide precision bounds for observables under perturbations; this work extends them to the quantum domain for continuously monitored open systems.
method: Uses the Lindblad master equation and quantum jump formalism to derive a kinetic uncertainty relation that bounds the response of steady-state observables to perturbations.
result: Obtains a quantum version of the response kinetic uncertainty relation, linking the sensitivity of observables to the dynamical activity and entropy production.
conclusion: The derived relation provides a fundamental thermodynamic bound on the precision of response in quantum systems, with implications for quantum sensing and thermodynamics.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series data using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic properties from experimental time-series data is challenging; the authors aim to learn thermodynamic quantities without prior knowledge of the system's dynamics.
method: They introduce a framework based on correlation currents and trajectory-fluctuation currents, leveraging machine learning to extract thermodynamic information from observed trajectories.
result: The method successfully reconstructs entropy production, free energy differences, and other thermodynamic quantities from simulated and experimental data.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for inferring thermodynamics in small systems, bridging data-driven analysis and stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between measurements and quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing and for characterizing measurement-induced phases.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions corresponding to different decoding phases.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and have implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using doped Clifford circuits requires extensive non-Clifford resources, establishing fundamental lower bounds on the T-count.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of pseudorandomness is crucial for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments, where Clifford circuits with few non-Clifford gates are a leading candidate.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including stabilizer formalism and magic state resource theory, to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates needed to achieve approximate unitary designs.
result: They show that any circuit that approximates a unitary 2-design to within constant error must have a non-Clifford gate count that scales linearly with the number of qubits, implying extensive doping is necessary.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental limitation on the efficiency of generating pseudorandom unitaries with Clifford circuits, with implications for quantum cryptography and benchmarking.

title: Entanglement Transition In Unitary System-Bath Dynamics
authors: Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, And Dario Poletti
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, and Dario Poletti

The evolution of a system coupled to baths is commonly described by a master equation that, in the long-time limit, yields a steady-state density matrix. However, when the same evolution is unraveled into quantum trajectories, it is possible to observe a transition in the scaling of entanglement wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240401] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers an entanglement transition in the steady-state of a system coupled to baths, revealed by unraveling the master equation into quantum trajectories.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement behaves in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, but typical master equations only yield steady-state density matrices that may hide dynamical entanglement features.
method: The authors study a system-bath model using a quantum trajectory approach, where the master equation is unraveled into stochastic pure-state evolutions, and analyze the scaling of entanglement entropy with system size.
result: They find a transition in the entanglement scaling from area-law to volume-law as a function of the measurement rate or coupling strength, analogous to measurement-induced phase transitions in monitored circuits.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that entanglement transitions can occur in unitary system-bath dynamics without explicit measurements, linking open quantum systems to the physics of quantum trajectories and measurement-induced phases.

title: Nonstabilizerness And Error Resilience In Noisy Quantum Circuits
authors: Fabian Ballar Trigueros And José Antonio Marín Guzmán
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Ballar Trigueros and José Antonio Marín Guzmán

We investigate how noise impacts nonstabilizerness—a key resource for quantum advantage—in many-body qubit systems. While noise typically degrades quantum resources, we show that amplitude damping, a nonunital channel, can generate or enhance nonstabilizerness, whereas depolarizing noise provably ca…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240602] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how noise affects nonstabilizerness (magic) in many-body qubit systems, finding that amplitude damping can generate or enhance it while depolarizing noise cannot.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its behavior under noise is poorly understood; understanding this is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the effect of amplitude damping and depolarizing noise on nonstabilizerness in many-body qubit systems, using theoretical proofs and numerical simulations.
result: Amplitude damping, a nonunital channel, can generate or enhance nonstabilizerness, whereas depolarizing noise provably cannot.
conclusion: Noise is not always detrimental to quantum resources; certain nonunital noise channels can actually boost nonstabilizerness, which has implications for error resilience and resource theory.

title: Theory Of Quantum Comb Enhanced Interferometry
authors: Haowei Shi And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Haowei Shi and Quntao Zhuang

Optical frequency combs, named for their comblike peaks in the spectrum, are essential for various sensing applications. As the technology develops, its performance has reached the standard quantum limit dictated by the quantum fluctuations of coherent light field. Quantum combs, with their quantum …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243602] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of quantum comb enhanced interferometry, showing how quantum combs can surpass the standard quantum limit for sensing.
motivation: Optical frequency combs are essential for sensing but are limited by the standard quantum limit; quantum combs offer a path to enhanced performance.
method: The authors formulate a general theory of quantum combs, analyzing their quantum properties and deriving bounds on measurement precision using quantum Fisher information.
result: Quantum combs can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in interferometry, outperforming classical combs and coherent states.
conclusion: Quantum combs provide a practical resource for quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in precision sensing.

title: Compensating Random Transition-Detection Blackouts In Markov Networks
authors: Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, And Udo Seifert
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, and Udo Seifert

In Markov networks, measurement blackouts with unknown frequency compromise observations such that thermodynamic quantities can no longer be inferred reliably. In particular, the observed currents neither discern equilibrium from nonequilibrium nor can they be used in extant estimators of entropy pr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 247101] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper addresses how to infer thermodynamic quantities from Markov networks when measurements suffer from random blackouts, proposing a method to compensate for missing data.
motivation: Measurement blackouts in Markov networks prevent reliable inference of thermodynamic quantities like entropy production, hindering the detection of nonequilibrium behavior.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to estimate currents and entropy production from incomplete observations by modeling the blackout process and using statistical inference.
result: They show that even with random blackouts, it is possible to distinguish equilibrium from nonequilibrium and accurately estimate entropy production using their compensation method.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing experimental data with missing measurements, extending the applicability of thermodynamic inference to realistic scenarios.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anticoncentration and state design properties of real Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources, using Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of random quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and benchmarking; here the focus is on real Clifford circuits, which are relevant to many quantum computing platforms.
method: The authors develop the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group and derive exact overlap distributions of real stabilizer states, analyzing the effect of doping with non-Clifford resources.
result: They identify a different universality class for real stabilizer states compared to complex ones, and characterize the emergence of approximate state designs and anticoncentration.
conclusion: Real Clifford circuits with magic resources can achieve anticoncentration and form approximate state designs, but with distinct statistical properties that may impact quantum advantage claims.

title: Non-Hermitian Cavity Magnomechanics With $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry-related Asymmetric Transparency
authors: Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, And Kashif Ammar Yasir
abstract:
Author(s): Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, and Kashif Ammar Yasir

We investigate magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling. The setup consists of a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere, where the magnon mode is further hybridized w…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063522] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with non-Hermitian coupling, revealing PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian physics and PT-symmetry in hybrid quantum systems, specifically cavity magnomechanics, and to understand the resulting asymmetric transparency phenomena.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling, using input-output formalism and solving for transmission spectra.
result: Demonstrates that non-Hermitian coupling leads to asymmetric magnomechanically induced transparency, controllable by the coupling phase and strength.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-Hermitian effects in hybrid quantum systems and may have applications in quantum information processing and sensing.

title: Remote Nonreciprocal Optical-microwave Entanglement And One-way Steering Via Parametric Amplification
authors: Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, And Hao Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, and Hao Xiong

We propose a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between spatially separated optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification. Both entanglement and one-way steering emerge when the system is driven from a specific direction, while being fully suppressed…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063730] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification in a hybrid system.
motivation: To achieve directional quantum correlations between optical and microwave fields, which is crucial for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses parametric amplification in a cavity optomechanical system with a nonlinear crystal to create nonreciprocal entanglement and steering.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and one-way steering occur only when driven from a specific direction, and are suppressed otherwise.
conclusion: The scheme provides a way to control quantum correlations directionally, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum networks.

title: Almost Sure Minimality Of The Set Of Experiments With Classical Kirkwood-Dirac Representations
authors: Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan de Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, And David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan De Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, and David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

A central problem in quantum information is determining quantum-classical boundaries. In the quasiprobability framework, a state is called classical if it is represented by a quasiprobability distribution that is positive, and thus a probability distribution. In recent years, the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD)…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062215] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the set of quantum experiments with classical Kirkwood-Dirac representations is almost surely minimal, establishing a sharp quantum-classical boundary.
motivation: Determining when a quantum state can be described by a classical probability distribution is a central problem in quantum information. The Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability representation offers a framework to study this boundary.
method: The authors use measure-theoretic arguments and properties of the Kirkwood-Dirac distribution to characterize the set of experiments (POVMs and states) that yield positive KD distributions, showing that this set is of measure zero in the space of all experiments.
result: They prove that the set of experiments with classical KD representations is almost surely minimal, meaning that almost all experiments yield non-positive KD distributions, thus exhibiting genuine quantum features.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous characterization of the quantum-classical divide in the KD framework, highlighting the rarity of classicality and reinforcing the non-classical nature of most quantum experiments.

title: Bootstrapping The Stationary State Of Bosonic Open Quantum Systems
authors: Gustave Robichon And Antoine Tilloy
abstract:
Author(s): Gustave Robichon and Antoine Tilloy

We propose a method to compute expectation values of observables in the stationary state of a (Markovian) bosonic open quantum system. Using a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations, we obtain finer and finer upper and lower bounds to any expectation value of interest. The bounds are rigorous, robust…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A method to compute stationary expectation values of bosonic open quantum systems using semidefinite relaxations, providing rigorous bounds.
motivation: Computing stationary states of bosonic open quantum systems is challenging due to infinite Hilbert spaces; existing methods lack rigorous error bounds.
method: The authors formulate a hierarchy of semidefinite programs that yield converging upper and lower bounds on expectation values of observables in the steady state.
result: The method produces rigorous, robust bounds that improve with hierarchy level, demonstrated on examples like the Kerr oscillator.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical and rigorous way to characterize stationary states of bosonic open systems, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and quantum optics.

title: Enhancing Collective Spin Squeezing Via One-axis-twisting Echo Control Of Individual Atoms
authors: Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, And Yanhong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, and Yanhong Xiao

Spin squeezing generated via interatom entanglement in multilevel atomic ensembles provides a powerful resource for quantum-enhanced metrology. Existing schemes that harness internal atomic degrees of freedom to boost squeezing typically encode the collective squeezing in complex superpositions of m…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062809] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a one-axis-twisting echo control method to enhance collective spin squeezing in multilevel atomic ensembles, improving metrological gain.
motivation: Existing spin squeezing schemes using internal atomic degrees of freedom suffer from limited squeezing due to decoherence and complexity. The authors aim to develop a simpler and more robust protocol.
method: They introduce a one-axis-twisting echo sequence that refocuses inhomogeneous broadening and decoherence in a multilevel atomic ensemble, combined with optical pumping to prepare the initial state.
result: The protocol achieves significantly enhanced spin squeezing compared to standard one-axis-twisting, with improved robustness against experimental imperfections.
conclusion: This echo-based control provides a practical route to generate strong spin squeezing in atomic ensembles, benefiting quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Geometric Invariants Of Quantum Metrology
authors: Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, and Murray J. Holland

We establish a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) expressed as follows; when the QFIM is constructed from a set of observables closed under commutation, i.e., a Lie algebra, the spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary dynamics generated by these same operators.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063725] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) when constructed from a Lie algebra, showing its spectrum is invariant under unitary dynamics.
motivation: Quantum Fisher information is central to quantum metrology, but its geometric invariants under dynamics were not well understood. Understanding these invariants can lead to more robust metrological protocols.
method: The authors consider the QFIM built from a set of observables that form a Lie algebra. They prove that the spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under any unitary evolution generated by the same algebra, using algebraic and information-geometric arguments.
result: The spectrum of the QFIM is a conserved quantity under the dynamics generated by the Lie algebra. This provides a geometric invariant that characterizes the metrological power of the system.
conclusion: This conservation law offers a new tool for analyzing quantum metrology protocols, potentially enabling the design of optimal measurements that are robust to certain dynamical changes.

title: Limitations Of Quantum Measurements And Operations Of Scattering Type Under The Energy Conservation Law
authors: Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, And Masahiro Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, and Masahiro Hotta

It is important to improve the accuracy of quantum measurements and operations both in engineering and fundamental physics. It is known, however, that the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations is generally limited by conservation laws according to the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062214] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental limits on quantum measurements and operations of scattering type under energy conservation, extending the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem.
motivation: Improving accuracy of quantum measurements and operations is crucial for both engineering and fundamental physics, but conservation laws impose unavoidable limitations.
method: The authors analyze scattering-type quantum measurements and operations, applying the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem and developing new bounds based on energy conservation.
result: They obtain trade-off relations between the accuracy of measurements/operations and the energy uncertainty of the apparatus, generalizing previous results.
conclusion: Energy conservation fundamentally restricts the achievable accuracy of scattering-type quantum processes, with implications for quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Qudit Encoding In Rydberg-blockaded Arrays Of Atoms
authors: Achille Robert And Tom Bienaimé
abstract:
Author(s): Achille Robert and Tom Bienaimé

We propose a protocol to realize arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit encoded in the collective dressed states of a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms. This system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model and acts as a multilevel Rydberg superatom whose nonlinear s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062614] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for qudit encoding and universal control using collective dressed states in a Rydberg-blockaded atomic array, isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: To realize high-dimensional quantum information processing (qudits) in a scalable atomic platform, leveraging Rydberg blockade for collective encoding.
method: Uses a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms to create a multilevel superatom, with control via external fields to perform arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations.
result: Demonstrates that the system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model, enabling nonlinear operations and qudit manipulation with high fidelity.
conclusion: The proposed protocol offers a viable path for qudit-based quantum computing in neutral atom arrays, with potential for scalability and error correction.

title: Photon-mediated Hybridization And Dissipative Transport In A cavity-QED Ring-acceptor Architecture
authors: Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, And Sarben Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, and Sarben Sarkar

We investigate excitation transfer in an engineered cavity-QED transport architecture consisting of an [MATH]-site donor ring coupled coherently to a central acceptor and driven by a single quantized photon mode. The system evolves under a Lindblad master equation including spontaneous loss and pure de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063721] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies excitation transfer in a cavity-QED ring-acceptor architecture driven by a single photon mode, focusing on dissipative transport and hybridization.
motivation: Understanding photon-mediated energy transport in engineered quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The system is modeled using a Lindblad master equation that includes spontaneous loss and pure dephasing, and the dynamics are analyzed to study hybridization and transport.
result: The authors find that the cavity mode mediates hybridization between the donor ring and acceptor, and that dissipation leads to steady-state transport properties.
conclusion: The cavity-QED architecture provides a controllable platform for studying quantum transport and may have applications in quantum networks and energy transfer.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, revealing a gauge structure in statistical response functions.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints like sum rules and Ward identities are hard to expose due to distributional currents and anomaly-like contact terms; a unified geometric organization is needed.
method: The authors develop a geometric approach based on a statistical-gauge connection, organizing response functions and constraints in a gauge-theoretic language.
result: They show that equilibrium constraints arise from a gauge structure, providing a systematic way to derive sum rules and Ward identities.
conclusion: This geometric perspective offers a powerful tool for analyzing quantum many-body systems at equilibrium, with potential applications to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a consistent thermodynamic description was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings using a field-theoretic approach and path integrals.
