result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and shows that entropy production can be decomposed into contributions from reciprocal and nonreciprocal parts.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent way to model nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Miniature Work-to-work Converter Engine Powered By Motor Protein
authors: Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, And Sudipto Muhuri
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, and Sudipto Muhuri

Designing a miniature microscale engine that can override the role of thermal fluctuations has remained elusive and is an important open challenge. Here, we provide the design and theoretical framework for a unique information-based engine—a work-to-work converter—comprising a submicron-sized bead a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064407] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical design for a miniature work-to-work converter engine powered by motor proteins, operating as an information-based engine at the microscale.
motivation: Designing a microscale engine that can override thermal fluctuations is an open challenge; this work aims to provide a theoretical framework for such an engine.
method: The authors propose a design involving a submicron-sized bead and motor proteins, and develop a theoretical framework for an information-based work-to-work converter.
result: The paper presents a unique engine design that can convert work from one form to another at the microscale, potentially overcoming thermal fluctuations.
conclusion: The proposed engine demonstrates a viable approach to microscale work conversion, with implications for nanoscale thermodynamics and bio-inspired machines.

title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of quantum Hamiltonians is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics, but existing methods are often inefficient for topologically ordered systems like the toric code.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the toric code Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, enabling efficient Gibbs sampling using classical Monte Carlo methods.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial resources, and the duality provides a rigorous bound on the mixing time of the quantum Gibbs sampler.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient approach to Gibbs state preparation for topologically ordered systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations using simple molecular systems, relevant to the origins of life.
motivation: To understand how primitive life could harvest energy without complex enzymatic machinery, by exploiting cyclic changes in the environment.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of a chemical system driven by periodic variations in environmental parameters, analyzing energy extraction via stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They show that cyclic environments can enable net work extraction from chemical reactions, with efficiency depending on the cycle frequency and reaction kinetics.
conclusion: Cyclic environmental changes provide a robust physical mechanism for chemical energy harvesting, offering insights into prebiotic energy transduction.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis states are used for robust entangled differential phase sensing, offering common-mode noise insensitivity for quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a robust quantum-enhanced approach using entangled states.
method: The paper proposes using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles, to perform differential phase sensing. These states are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, and the authors analyze their performance under realistic conditions.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states like spin-squeezed states.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments, with potential applications in quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of Fock states and squeezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: The technique provides a versatile tool for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from low secret key rates and security proofs that are not composable. The authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and optimize the protocol parameters for high key rates over fiber.
result: The protocol achieves record-high secret key rates for CV-QKD over metropolitan distances, with rigorous composable security guarantees.
conclusion: This work brings CV-QKD closer to practical deployment by demonstrating that high rates and composable security are simultaneously achievable.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique advances the use of circular Rydberg atoms in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization and characterize the excited-state dynamics, providing insights into the loss of qubit fidelity.
conclusion: The findings contribute to improving transmon qubit readout and overall performance in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging error correction even with shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing; radiation-induced errors are a known but poorly characterized noise source.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, using a custom setup to isolate radiation effects.
result: They observe correlated phase error bursts that occur simultaneously across multiple qubits, with rates that persist despite state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation pose a fundamental challenge to quantum error correction, requiring new mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in quantum circuits, studying the breakdown of shadowing and the nature of the Trotterization transition.
result: Shadowing time is finite for many-body chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit, being a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the limits of Trotterization and the onset of thermalization, with implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduced model that preserves relevant dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to define a coarse-grained time step and derive an effective reduced dynamics.
result: The technique accurately reproduces the observable dynamics of the original system while significantly reducing computational cost.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems, bridging microscopic models and observed dynamics.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, performing spectroscopy and noise characterization to identify mechanisms causing spectral diffusion and linewidth broadening.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability, including charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence effects.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon show promise for quantum networking, but further material and device engineering is needed to achieve transform-limited linewidths.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The method accurately identifies the number and parameters of spin baths in simulated and experimental NV center data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient, scalable tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with direct application to hybrid quantum systems like NV centers.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve strong blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission, even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up adiabatic quantum processes, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action approach combined with computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling systematic improvement of the driving fields.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity for quantum state preparation and control compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and readily available upgrade for quantum control, with potential applications in quantum computing and thermodynamics.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or target only uncorrelated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local decoupling sequences.
result: They demonstrate that the sequence length depends only on the locality k of the noise, not on the total number of qubits, and provide explicit constructions.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering efficient noise suppression for spatially correlated errors in large quantum systems.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it is crucial for reaching the standard quantum limit and beyond.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a system that mimics a mechanical oscillator with negative effective mass.
result: They demonstrate coherent cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps, analyzing their error scaling and resource requirements for phase estimation.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude reduction in the number of Trotter steps needed for given accuracy, with rigorous bounds on the success probability and phase estimation error.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, with immediate applications in quantum chemistry and beyond.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements often disturb the system, limiting the ability to perform repeated or sequential measurements. Nondemolition measurements are crucial for quantum error correction and state preparation.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize back-action, using a silicon spin qudit as a testbed.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qubit platforms.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations improves simulation accuracy sevenfold for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors, likely using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise models can significantly enhance the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, aiding in algorithm development and error mitigation.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade performance; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally observe suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, demonstrating a protected idle gate.
conclusion: This approach provides a simple and effective method to mitigate leakage in exchange-only qubits, advancing their viability for quantum computing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the thermodynamic behavior of quantum systems, which is a core interest in information thermodynamics.
method: The authors use repeated interventions to construct projected ensembles of process tensors, which capture the influence of measurements on the dynamics, and analyze their properties to detect chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble approach can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics and provides a unified framework for various chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for probing quantum chaos, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and the study of thermalization in many-body systems.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving parity dynamics for Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.
motivation: To realize Majorana-based qubits, fast and noninvasive readout of parity states in minimal Kitaev chain devices is essential.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry on a hybrid superconductor-semiconductor nanowire device to probe charge and parity dynamics.
result: They demonstrate readout of key processes and parity dynamics, showing the feasibility of this technique for Kitaev chain qubits.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a promising tool for scalable readout in topological quantum computing platforms.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods for quantum communication, including compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and higher secret key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, reconciliation) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, CV quantum networks, and related protocols.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and rates, and continuous-variable entanglement distribution is advancing toward real-world quantum networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing challenges in security proofs and hardware integration.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: It provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with focus on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are ubiquitous in modern experiments, yet their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify stationary states and universal scaling regimes, emphasizing symmetry and topology.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to concepts like topological order and purity transitions.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory on nonequilibrium quantum phases.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, using quantum information methods to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum theories of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks based on entanglement and information theory, and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between quantum probes.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for testing quantum gravity via entanglement generation.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a promising path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with several feasible tabletop experiments on the horizon.

title: Quantum Mechanics Based On Real Numbers: A Consistent Description
authors: Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, And Dagmar Bruß
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, and Dagmar Bruß

By exploiting a physically motivated principle, rather than a mathematical postulate, researchers offer a new perspective on how a real-valued quantum theory can be constructed.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240202] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs a consistent real-valued quantum theory based on a physically motivated principle, challenging the necessity of complex numbers in quantum mechanics.
motivation: To determine whether complex numbers are essential for a consistent formulation of quantum mechanics or if a real-valued theory can suffice.
method: The authors propose a physically motivated principle (e.g., no-signaling or operational constraints) to derive a real-valued quantum theory and test its consistency with known quantum phenomena.
result: They show that a real-valued quantum theory can be constructed that reproduces many predictions of standard quantum mechanics, though it may differ in certain multipartite scenarios.
conclusion: Complex numbers are not strictly necessary for a consistent quantum description, but real-valued theories impose additional constraints that may be testable experimentally.

title: Quantum State Preparation Without Coherent Arithmetic
authors: Sam Mcardle, András Gilyén, And Mario Berta
abstract:
Author(s): Sam McArdle, András Gilyén, and Mario Berta

We introduce a versatile method for preparing a quantum state whose amplitudes are given by some known function. Unlike existing approaches, our method does not require handcrafted reversible arithmetic circuits, or quantum table reads, to encode the function values. Instead, we use a template quant…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240603] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing quantum states with amplitudes given by a known function without coherent arithmetic or table lookups.
motivation: Existing state preparation methods require expensive reversible arithmetic circuits or quantum table lookups, which are resource-intensive. This work aims to reduce the quantum resource cost.
method: The method uses a template quantum circuit that can be adjusted via classical optimization to approximate the target function, avoiding coherent arithmetic.
result: The approach achieves efficient state preparation with lower gate counts and qubit requirements compared to traditional methods, demonstrated for several functions.
conclusion: The technique offers a practical alternative for state preparation in quantum algorithms, particularly useful for near-term quantum devices.

title: Universal Two-Excitation Scattering In Two-Dimensional Subwavelength Atomic Arrays
authors: Yidan Wang (王艺丹), Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Valentin Walther, And Susanne F. Yelin
abstract:
Author(s): Yidan Wang (王艺丹), Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Valentin Walther, and Susanne F. Yelin

Subwavelength atomic arrays are a leading platform for engineering strong light-matter interactions, presenting exciting opportunities for quantum science. However, a full understanding of their multiexcitation dynamics remains a significant challenge. In this Letter, we uncover a remarkable univers…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243603] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals universal two-excitation scattering behavior in subwavelength atomic arrays, showing that the scattering matrix depends only on the number of atoms and not on the array geometry.
motivation: Understanding multiexcitation dynamics in subwavelength atomic arrays is crucial for quantum science applications, but a full theoretical description has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the spin model and Green's function approach to compute two-excitation scattering amplitudes for various array geometries.
result: They find that the two-excitation scattering matrix is universal, depending only on the number of atoms, and derive analytical expressions for the scattering amplitudes.
conclusion: This universality simplifies the description of multiexcitation dynamics and may enable new quantum protocols in atomic arrays.

title: State- Versus Reaction-Based Information Processing In Biochemical Networks
authors: Anne-Lena Moor, Age Tjalma, Manuel Reinhardt, Pieter Rein Ten Wolde, And Christoph Zechner
abstract:
Author(s): Anne-Lena Moor, Age Tjalma, Manuel Reinhardt, Pieter Rein ten Wolde, and Christoph Zechner

Trajectory mutual information is frequently used to quantify information transfer in biochemical systems. Tractable solutions of the trajectory mutual information can be obtained via the widely used linear-noise approximation (LNA) using Gaussian channel theory. This approach is expected to be accur…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248401] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes information processing in biochemical networks using trajectory mutual information and the linear-noise approximation, connecting to thermodynamic constraints.
motivation: Understanding how biochemical networks process information is crucial for cellular function, but quantifying information transfer in stochastic systems is challenging.
method: The authors use the linear-noise approximation (LNA) to compute trajectory mutual information in biochemical networks, treating them as Gaussian channels.
result: They derive tractable expressions for mutual information and show that the LNA accurately captures information transfer in certain regimes, revealing trade-offs between state- and reaction-based information.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for analyzing information processing in biochemical networks, with implications for the thermodynamics of information in biological systems.

title: Parent Hamiltonians For Stabilizer Quantum Many-Body Scars
authors: Shane Dooley
abstract:
Author(s): Shane Dooley

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) have attracted considerable interest due to their role in weak ergodicity breaking in many-body systems. We present a general construction that embeds stabilizer states as QMBS of local Hamiltonians. The method relies on a notion of factorizability of Pauli strings on …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240402] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A general construction to embed stabilizer states as quantum many-body scars in local Hamiltonians.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars provide a mechanism for weak ergodicity breaking, and embedding stabilizer states as scars could enable controlled non-thermal behavior.
method: The construction uses factorizability of Pauli strings to design parent Hamiltonians whose eigenstates include stabilizer states as scars.
result: Stabilizer states can be realized as exact eigenstates (scars) of local Hamiltonians, with the method generalizing to any stabilizer state.
conclusion: This work provides a systematic way to embed known quantum information states into many-body Hamiltonians, bridging quantum information and condensed matter physics.

title: Nonreciprocal Universal Photon Blockade In An Asymmetrical Cavity
authors: Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, And Yaping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, and Yaping Yang

Inspired by the distinctive properties of universal photon blockade (UPB), we propose a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve quantum nonreciprocity. Through theoretical analysis, we establish direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect UPB in weak-driving limita…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063729] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve nonreciprocal universal photon blockade.
motivation: Universal photon blockade (UPB) is a key effect for quantum information processing, but achieving nonreciprocal behavior is challenging. This work aims to realize direction-dependent UPB using an asymmetrical cavity.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity, deriving optimal conditions for perfect UPB under weak driving. They use quantum master equation and input-output formalism.
result: They find direction-dependent optimal conditions for UPB, enabling nonreciprocal photon blockade where transmission is blocked in one direction but not the other.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a way to achieve quantum nonreciprocity via UPB, which could be useful for quantum diodes and other quantum network components.

title: Effects Of Static Dc Electric-field Orientation On Two-photon Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas Destefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, And Irina Novikova
abstract:
Author(s): Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas DeStefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, and Irina Novikova

We examine the influence of a static dc electric field on electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances that involve highly excited Rydberg states. Our focus is on how these resonances are altered when the relative orientation between the laser polarization and the external electric-fiel…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062619] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the orientation of a static DC electric field affects two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances.
motivation: Understanding the influence of electric field orientation on Rydberg EIT is important for applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems where Rydberg atoms are coupled to other platforms.
method: The authors experimentally measure EIT spectra in a Rydberg atomic vapor cell while varying the direction of an applied DC electric field relative to the laser polarization.
result: They find that the EIT resonance line shape and strength depend significantly on the field orientation, consistent with theoretical models of Stark shifts and transition dipole moments.
conclusion: The results highlight the need to control electric field orientation in Rydberg-based quantum devices and provide insights for optimizing hybrid quantum systems involving Rydberg atoms.

title: Application And Quantum Properties Of Superpositions Of Oppositely Squeezed States
authors: Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, And Kae Nemoto
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, and Kae Nemoto

We show that superpositions of oppositely squeezed states—non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states—exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime. These states possess photon-number structures distinct from conventional coherent-state cat s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063728] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime.
motivation: To explore non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states that may offer advantages for quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the photon-number structure and nonclassical properties of superpositions of oppositely squeezed states, and study their entanglement advantage.
result: These states show enhanced nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime.
conclusion: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are promising non-Gaussian resources for quantum information tasks.

title: Tighter Asymptotic Key Rates For Intensity-correlated Decoy-state Quantum Key Distribution Via Nonlinear Programming
authors: Matej Pivoluska And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Pivoluska and Mateus Araújo

Decoy-state QKD with phase-randomized weak coherent pulses is typically analyzed assuming independent, precisely prepared intensities. Real sources, however, can exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, potentially leaking intensity information and breaking the standard decoy-state reductio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062441] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves asymptotic key rate bounds for decoy-state QKD with intensity correlations using nonlinear programming.
motivation: Real QKD sources have correlated intensity drifts that compromise security; standard decoy-state analysis assumes independent intensities, so tighter bounds are needed.
method: The authors formulate the key rate optimization as a nonlinear programming problem that accounts for intensity correlations, and solve it to obtain tighter asymptotic bounds.
result: They demonstrate significantly higher key rates compared to conventional analysis under realistic intensity correlation models.
conclusion: Nonlinear programming provides a practical way to incorporate source imperfections and improve QKD performance, making decoy-state QKD more robust.

title: Optimal Control Of Open-quantum-system Dynamics Predicted By Long Short-term Memory
authors: Jun-Dong Zhong And Zhao-Ming Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Dong Zhong and Zhao-Ming Wang

The realization of high-fidelity quantum control is crucial for quantum information processing, particularly in noisy environments where control strategies must simultaneously achieve precise manipulation and effective noise suppression. Conventional optimal control designs typically require numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062442] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Uses long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to predict optimal control pulses for open quantum systems, achieving high-fidelity control in noisy environments.
motivation: Conventional optimal control for open quantum systems is computationally expensive; machine learning offers a faster alternative for predicting control strategies.
method: Trains an LSTM network on data from optimal control solutions (e.g., GRAPE) to predict control pulses for given system parameters and noise conditions.
result: The LSTM-based approach predicts control pulses with high fidelity, significantly reducing computation time compared to traditional numerical optimization.
conclusion: Machine learning, specifically LSTM, can efficiently predict optimal quantum control for open systems, aiding practical quantum information processing.

title: Increasing Entanglement Concentration And The Role Of Measurement Imaginarity
authors: Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, And Debasis Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, and Debasis Sarkar

The role of complex numbers in quantum theory extends beyond mathematical convenience, having recently been formalized as a resource under the framework of the resource theory of imaginarity. Operationally, imaginarity translates into using more resources in linear optical setups. In this work, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062439] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how the imaginarity of measurements affects entanglement concentration, showing that using complex-valued measurements can increase the success probability of extracting maximally entangled states from partially entangled ones.
motivation: Understanding the role of complex numbers in quantum operations is fundamental, and imaginarity has been identified as a resource. The authors aim to explore whether imaginarity in measurements can enhance entanglement concentration protocols.
method: The authors consider a general entanglement concentration protocol using local operations and classical communication, and analyze the success probability as a function of the imaginarity of the measurement operators. They derive bounds and provide examples.
result: They find that increasing the imaginarity of measurements can increase the success probability of entanglement concentration, and they quantify this relationship. The results are illustrated with specific two-qubit states.
conclusion: Imaginarity in measurements is a useful resource for entanglement concentration, and the work highlights the operational significance of complex numbers in quantum information processing.

title: Demonstration Of The Universal Intrinsic Higher-rank Spin Tensor Hall Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, And Yiheng Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, and Yiheng Lin

The spin Hall effect enables pure spin-current generation without charge transport. Notably, its intrinsic contribution, originating from spin-orbit coupling, can exhibit universal values that are robust against parameter fluctuations. Recent extensions of this effect to high-spin systems predict ri…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062616] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect using a trapped ion system.
motivation: To extend the spin Hall effect to high-spin systems and observe universal behavior robust against parameter fluctuations.
method: Uses a trapped ion platform to simulate spin-orbit coupling and measure spin tensor currents.
result: Observes the predicted universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect.
conclusion: Trapped ions provide a versatile platform for studying higher-rank spin transport phenomena.

title: Tunable Bundle Emissions Of $n$-phonon And Photon-phonon Pairs Via The Barnett Effect
authors: Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, And Zhi-Rong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, and Zhi-Rong Zhong

We theoretically propose a scheme for the generation of [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions in a cavity magnomechanics system. By utilizing the Barnett effect under resonant driving, [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations can be achieved. Through the system's dissipative…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063722] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a cavity magnomechanics system to generate n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions via the Barnett effect.
motivation: To achieve tunable bundle emissions of phonons and photon-phonon pairs, which are important for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses the Barnett effect under resonant driving in a cavity magnomechanics system to induce n-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations, then relies on dissipative dynamics to generate bundle emissions.
result: Demonstrates that n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions can be generated and tuned by controlling system parameters.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new method for generating nonclassical states in hybrid magnomechanical systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and sensing.

title: Strong Coupling Of Excitons In Monolayer ${\mathrm{WS}}_{2}$ With Brillouin Zone Folding Induced Quasibound States In The Continuum
authors: Xiongwei Guo, Yingying Zhang, Jinhai Si, Xun Hou, And Kuidong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongwei Guo, Yingying Zhang, Jinhai Si, Xun Hou, and Kuidong Wang

All-dielectric optical metasurfaces that supporting optical quasibound states in the continuum (QBICs) offer a promising platform in realization of strong light-matter coupling with monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs). Such coupled systems are critical for wide range of applications i…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235425] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Strong coupling between excitons in monolayer WS2 and quasibound states in the continuum in an all-dielectric metasurface is demonstrated.
motivation: Strong light-matter coupling with monolayer TMDCs is important for applications in quantum optics and optoelectronics, but achieving it with high quality factors is challenging.
method: The authors design an all-dielectric metasurface supporting quasibound states in the continuum (QBICs) and couple it to monolayer WS2 excitons, measuring the optical response.
result: They observe clear Rabi splitting, indicating strong coupling with a Rabi energy of ~30 meV, and show that the QBIC resonances enhance the coupling strength.
conclusion: All-dielectric metasurfaces with QBICs provide a robust platform for strong coupling with TMDC excitons, promising for quantum hybrid systems.

title: Coherent Perfect Absorption Of Anti-modes In An Indirect Coupled Magnon-polariton System
authors: Chenyang Lu, Jiguang Yao, Jiongjie Wang, Jiang Xiao, And Can-Ming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Chenyang Lu, Jiguang Yao, Jiongjie Wang, Jiang Xiao, and Can-Ming Hu

In this work, we report coherent perfect absorption (CPA) of anti-modes in an indirectly coupled magnon–polariton system. By examining both single and indirectly coupled cases, we experimentally distinguish the modal decay rate [MATH] from the effective decay rate [MATH]. At CPA, ${γ}_{\m…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224431] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports coherent perfect absorption of anti-modes in an indirectly coupled magnon-polariton system, distinguishing modal and effective decay rates.
motivation: Understanding and controlling absorption in hybrid magnon-polariton systems is important for quantum information processing and signal manipulation.
method: The authors experimentally study single and indirectly coupled magnon-polariton systems, measuring decay rates and demonstrating coherent perfect absorption.
result: They achieve coherent perfect absorption of anti-modes and experimentally distinguish the modal decay rate from the effective decay rate.
conclusion: The work provides insights into decay dynamics in hybrid systems and demonstrates a method for perfect absorption, which may be useful for quantum transducers and signal processing.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Shows that dynamical typicality holds for classical lattice systems with independent initial conditions, meaning macroscopic observables evolve close to their microcanonical average for most initial states.
motivation: To extend the concept of dynamical typicality, previously studied in quantum systems, to classical lattice systems, providing a rigorous foundation for equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: Analytical proof using probability theory and dynamical systems, assuming deterministic evolution and independent initial distributions for each lattice site.
result: For any macroscopic observable, the time evolution from typical initial conditions is well approximated by the microcanonical average, with deviations bounded by a small parameter inversely proportional to system size.
conclusion: Dynamical typicality is a general property of classical lattice systems, supporting the emergence of thermodynamic behavior from deterministic dynamics.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory is used to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating enhanced parameter estimation.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important for quantum information processing, but characterizing them is challenging. Machine learning offers a data-driven approach.
method: The authors implement a QELM where the reservoir is a quantum system with memory, processing sequential quantum states from a collision model to learn and estimate parameters of the non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The memory-enhanced QELM outperforms standard QELMs in estimating parameters like system-environment coupling strength and memory time, showing higher accuracy and robustness.
conclusion: Quantum reservoir computing with memory is a powerful tool for characterizing complex quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum metrology and control.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system, demonstrating its potential as a resource for quantum information processing.
motivation: ICO is a novel resource for quantum information, but most experiments have been photonic; exploring ICO in cavity QED systems could enable new applications.
method: The authors model two cavities coupled via a quantum switch, analyzing the resulting causal structure and information-theoretic properties.
result: They show that ICO can be realized in cavity QED, with measurable effects on quantum correlations and channel capacities.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, expanding the experimental toolbox for quantum information processing.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensation, a phase transition, can serve as a computational framework for cells to process high-dimensional environmental information.
motivation: Cells must process complex signals to respond appropriately, and traditional molecular circuits may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, nonlinear mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors draw analogies between phase separation in biomolecular condensates and computational primitives, discussing how condensates can sense, classify, and respond to multiple inputs simultaneously.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable high-dimensional information processing with minimal components, providing a new perspective on cellular computation.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation is a promising paradigm for understanding cellular information processing, with potential implications for synthetic biology and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: fast electronic cooling via quantum channels followed by slower relaxation due to nuclear spin interactions.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom governs thermalization, providing insights into heat dissipation in quantum devices.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to achieve nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to image atoms without destroying them, and use this technique to load atoms into arrays continuously. The experiment is performed in finite magnetic fields.
result: They achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and demonstrate continuous loading of atom arrays, which is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a practical and effective method for neutral-atom arrays, advancing the platform for quantum information processing.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction applications.
conclusion: The work advances neutral-atom platforms as viable candidates for fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing optimized multiqubit gates.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique fills a gap in qubit noise characterization, offering a practical tool for improving qubit coherence and understanding decoherence mechanisms.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction are still developing.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes, optimized for neutral-atom hardware with long-range interactions and native multi-qubit gates.
result: The architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit overhead, and runtime compared to conventional surface-code-based approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations.
conclusion: The transversal architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable platform for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation, bridging the gap between current hardware and practical quantum advantage.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how noise affects the concentration of loss functions in parametrized quantum circuits, linking expressivity to barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, and understanding the role of noise is crucial for practical training.
method: The authors derive theoretical bounds on loss function concentration under noise, using tools from random matrix theory and circuit complexity.
result: They show that noise can mitigate barren plateaus but at the cost of reduced expressivity, providing a trade-off relation.
conclusion: The results offer a principled guide for designing noisy quantum circuits that avoid barren plateaus while maintaining sufficient expressivity.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
