Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to simulate string-breaking dynamics in a quantum spin chain.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects and non-adiabatic transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for string breaking and highlights the role of quantum dynamics in confining systems, relevant for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with practical quantum chemistry computations, improving reliability despite hardware noise.
method: Implements noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets on a trapped-ion processor to compute molecular energies.
result: Achieves a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies, demonstrating improved accuracy over non-error-corrected approaches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry on current hardware, paving the way for reliable quantum simulations.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; this review aims to clarify and relate diverse approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various numerical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review systematically compares methods, highlighting their applicability, accuracy, and computational cost for different parameter regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems, advancing both fundamental understanding and practical applications.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate complexity and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qudits can reduce the complexity of quantum circuits by replacing multiple qubits with a single higher-dimensional system, potentially simplifying hardware requirements and improving fidelity.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable more efficient decompositions of multiqubit gates, such as the Toffoli gate, and have been demonstrated in proof-of-principle experiments.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, but challenges remain in qudit control and error correction; further research is needed to realize practical advantages.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits.

title: Bootstrapping Quantum Hamiltonians With Symmetry
authors: Michael G. Scheer
abstract:
Author(s): Michael G. Scheer

We describe a semidefinite relaxation method which finds lower bounds to the ground state energy of a quantum Hamiltonian subject to Hermitian linear constraints along with approximations of ground state expectation values. We show that symmetry can be used to significantly reduce the computational …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246501] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A semidefinite relaxation method for bounding ground state energies of quantum Hamiltonians using symmetry reduction.
motivation: Computing ground state energies of quantum Hamiltonians is hard; symmetry can reduce complexity.
method: Formulates a semidefinite program that incorporates Hermitian linear constraints and symmetry to obtain lower bounds and approximate expectation values.
result: Demonstrates that symmetry significantly reduces computational cost while providing rigorous lower bounds.
conclusion: The method offers a practical tool for studying quantum many-body systems with symmetries.

title: Spin-Boson Mapping Of The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Sami Boulebnane, Abid Khan, Minzhao Liu, Jeffrey Larson, Dylan Herman, Ruslan Shaydulin, And Marco Pistoia
abstract:
Author(s): Sami Boulebnane, Abid Khan, Minzhao Liu, Jeffrey Larson, Dylan Herman, Ruslan Shaydulin, and Marco Pistoia

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) achieves monotonically improving performance with circuit depth [MATH], yet the study of the high-depth regime has been obstructed by the exponential in [MATH] cost of existing exact evaluation techniques. In this Letter, we prove that, in the infinite…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper maps the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to a spin-boson model to enable efficient evaluation of its performance at high circuit depths.
motivation: Exact evaluation of QAOA at high circuit depth is exponentially costly, hindering the study of its performance scaling. The authors aim to overcome this by exploiting a mapping to a spin-boson system.
method: The authors prove that in the infinite-size limit, the QAOA dynamics can be mapped to a spin-boson model, allowing the use of efficient techniques from condensed matter physics to compute expectation values.
result: The mapping yields a polynomial-time method to evaluate QAOA performance at any depth, revealing that the algorithm's performance saturates at a finite depth and does not improve monotonically beyond that.
conclusion: The spin-boson mapping provides a new tool for analyzing QAOA and suggests fundamental limits on its performance, with implications for quantum optimization.

title: Incoherent Repumping Scheme In The $^{88}\mathrm{Sr}^{+}$ Five-level Manifold
authors: Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, And Jean-Pierre Likforman
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, and Jean-Pierre Likforman

Laser-cooled trapped ions are at the heart of modern quantum technologies and their cooling dynamics often deviate from the simplified two-level atom model. Doppler cooling of the [MATH] ion involves several electronic levels and repumping channels that strongly influence fluorescenc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063109] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an incoherent repumping scheme for Doppler cooling of Sr+ ions, analyzing its effect on fluorescence and cooling dynamics.
motivation: Doppler cooling of trapped ions often involves multiple electronic levels and repumping channels, and understanding these dynamics is important for quantum technologies.
method: The authors model the five-level manifold of Sr+ and propose an incoherent repumping scheme, analyzing fluorescence spectra and cooling rates.
result: The incoherent repumping scheme modifies the fluorescence and cooling dynamics compared to coherent repumping, with potential implications for ion trap experiments.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new tool for controlling cooling in multi-level ions, but the paper is primarily an experimental technique paper without direct quantum information or thermodynamics focus.

title: Microwave-free Vector Magnetic-field Measurement Using A Single Nitrogen-vacancy-center Spin In Diamond
authors: Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, And Lumin Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, and Lumin Ji

Magnetic field sensors based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have attracted considerable attention due to their high sensitivity and spatial resolution. However, conventional vector magnetometry typically relies on either the four axes of ensemble NV centers or three orthogonal reference magnetic f…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062618] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A microwave-free vector magnetometry method using a single NV center in diamond is demonstrated.
motivation: Conventional NV-based vector magnetometry requires microwave fields or multiple NV axes, which can be limiting; a simpler, microwave-free approach is desired.
method: The authors use a single NV center and measure the Zeeman shifts of the spin sublevels via optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) without applying microwaves, relying on the intrinsic spin Hamiltonian and a bias magnetic field.
result: They achieve vector magnetic field measurement with high sensitivity and spatial resolution using only a single NV center and no microwave excitation.
conclusion: This technique simplifies NV-based vector magnetometry, potentially enabling more compact and low-power sensors.

title: Long-lived Metastable States In The $4{f}^{13}5d6s$ Configuration Of ${\mathrm{Yb}}^{+}$
authors: Z. E. D. Ackerman, A. Cadarso Quevedo, Ilango Maran, L. P. H. Gallagher, R. J. C. Spreeuw, J. C. Berengut, And R. Gerritsma
abstract:
Author(s): Z. E. D. Ackerman, A. Cadarso Quevedo, Ilango Maran, L. P. H. Gallagher, R. J. C. Spreeuw, J. C. Berengut, and R. Gerritsma

We study the occurrence of long-lived metastable states in the [MATH] electron configuration of [MATH]. By optical pumping of a single trapped ion on the [MATH] transition at 377.5 nm, we prepare a wide range of metastable electronic states…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062811] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-lived metastable states in the 4f13 5d 6s configuration of Yb+ ions, relevant for quantum information applications.
motivation: Understanding and controlling metastable states in Yb+ is important for applications in quantum computing and atomic clocks.
method: Optical pumping of a single trapped Yb+ ion on a specific transition at 377.5 nm is used to prepare and study metastable electronic states.
result: A wide range of long-lived metastable states are identified and characterized.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the electronic structure of Yb+ and its potential for quantum technologies.

title: Three-qubit-state Preparation: Classification And Explicit Circuits
authors: Yonghae Lee And Taewan Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Yonghae Lee and Taewan Kim

We develop a deterministic and fully explicit framework for preparing an arbitrary three-qubit pure state from its computational-basis amplitudes. Our approach exploits bipartite Schmidt structure: we classify three-qubit states into five types with respect to a [MATH] bipartition and provide concret…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062444] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A deterministic framework for preparing arbitrary three-qubit pure states using bipartite Schmidt decomposition and explicit quantum circuits.
motivation: Efficient state preparation is essential for quantum information processing, but explicit circuits for arbitrary three-qubit states are lacking.
method: Classifies three-qubit states into five types based on Schmidt rank across bipartitions and provides explicit circuit decompositions for each type.
result: Provides explicit quantum circuits for preparing any three-qubit pure state using at most 2 CNOT gates and single-qubit rotations.
conclusion: The framework offers a systematic and resource-efficient method for three-qubit state preparation, useful for quantum computing and communication.

title: Role Of Overparametrization In Quantum Approximate Optimization
authors: Daniil Rabinovich, Andrey Kardashin, And Soumik Adhikary
abstract:
Author(s): Daniil Rabinovich, Andrey Kardashin, and Soumik Adhikary

Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a cornerstone of contemporary quantum algorithms research. While they have demonstrated considerable promise in solving problems of practical interest, efficiently determining the minimal quantum resources necessary to obtain such a solution remains an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062617] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of overparametrization in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), showing that overparametrization can improve optimization but does not directly advance core quantum information theory.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms like QAOA are promising but require careful resource estimation; understanding overparametrization helps determine minimal quantum resources needed.
method: The authors analyze QAOA landscapes and training dynamics, comparing underparametrized and overparametrized regimes using numerical simulations and analytical arguments.
result: Overparametrization in QAOA leads to better optimization landscapes and avoids barren plateaus, but the benefits are limited to specific problem instances.
conclusion: While overparametrization aids optimization, it does not provide fundamental insights into quantum information theory or thermodynamics, and the work is more relevant to variational algorithm practice.

title: Unveiling Distinguishable non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, And Andrea Conti
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, and Andrea Conti

Quantum systems promise unprecedented performance with respect to classical counterparts for various applications involving sensing, communications, control, and computing. Bringing this promise to reality hinges upon the distinguishability between quantum states. This paper explores the distinguish…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062435] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores distinguishability of non-Gaussian quantum states, proposing a framework for quantifying state discrimination.
motivation: Distinguishing quantum states is crucial for quantum sensing, communication, and computing; non-Gaussian states are important for continuous-variable quantum information.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on quantum state discrimination theory, possibly using fidelity or other distance measures tailored to non-Gaussian states.
result: They identify conditions under which non-Gaussian states are distinguishable and quantify the advantage over Gaussian states.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of non-Gaussianity in quantum state discrimination, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Evolution Of Quantum State Texture Under Lorentz Transformations: Invariance, Competition, And Sensitivity In Single-particle And Bipartite Entangled Systems
authors: Zhiming Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiming Huang

Quantum state texture (QST), an emerging resource quantifying the global structural complexity of quantum states within a computational basis, exhibits dynamical behavior under relativistic frameworks that remains largely unexplored. This paper systematically investigates the evolution of QST under …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how quantum state texture evolves under Lorentz transformations in single-particle and bipartite entangled systems.
motivation: To understand the relativistic behavior of quantum state texture, a measure of global structural complexity, which has not been studied before.
method: Analytical and numerical calculations of quantum state texture under Lorentz boosts for single-particle and bipartite entangled states.
result: Quantum state texture is not Lorentz invariant; it shows competition between different basis contributions and sensitivity to boost parameters.
conclusion: Quantum state texture is a frame-dependent quantity, which may have implications for relativistic quantum information processing.

title: Krylov-space Anatomy And Spread Complexity Of A Disordered Quantum Spin Chain
authors: Bikram Pain, David E. Logan, And Sthitadhi Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Bikram Pain, David E. Logan, and Sthitadhi Roy

We investigate the anatomy and complexity of quantum states in Krylov space, in the ergodic and many-body localized (MBL) phases of a disordered, interacting spin chain. The Krylov basis generated by the Hamiltonian from an initial state provides a representation in which the spread of the time-evol…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214205] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Krylov-space anatomy and spread complexity of quantum states in a disordered spin chain, comparing ergodic and many-body localized phases.
motivation: Understanding the structure of quantum states in Krylov space can reveal signatures of ergodicity and localization, which are central to quantum thermalization.
method: The authors compute the Krylov basis generated by the Hamiltonian from an initial state and analyze the spread complexity, a measure of how the state spreads in Krylov space over time.
result: They find that spread complexity distinguishes ergodic and MBL phases, with ergodic phases showing faster and more extensive spread, while MBL phases exhibit slower, more confined spread.
conclusion: Krylov-space spread complexity provides a useful diagnostic for many-body localization and thermalization, but the paper does not directly address thermodynamic constraints or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Exact Multivalley Envelope Function Theory Of Valley Splitting In Si/SiGe Nanostructures
authors: Lasse Ermoneit, Abel Thayil, Thomas Koprucki, And Markus Kantner
abstract:
Author(s): Lasse Ermoneit, Abel Thayil, Thomas Koprucki, and Markus Kantner

Valley splitting in strained Si/SiGe quantum wells is a central parameter for silicon spin qubits and is commonly described with envelope function and effective mass theories. These models provide a computationally efficient continuum description and agree well with atomistic approaches when the con…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops an exact multivalley envelope function theory for valley splitting in Si/SiGe quantum wells, improving continuum models for spin qubit applications.
motivation: Valley splitting is critical for silicon spin qubits, but existing envelope function models lack accuracy compared to atomistic methods. An exact continuum theory is needed for efficient and reliable design.
method: The authors derive an exact multivalley envelope function theory by incorporating full zone-center Bloch functions and interface boundary conditions, avoiding common approximations.
result: The theory reproduces atomistic tight-binding results for valley splitting in Si/SiGe quantum wells with high accuracy, while retaining computational efficiency.
conclusion: The exact envelope function theory provides a validated continuum framework for valley splitting, enabling faster and more accurate simulations for silicon spin qubit design.

title: Quantum Hyperuniformity And Quantum Weight
authors: Junmo Jeon And Shiro Sakai
abstract:
Author(s): Junmo Jeon and Shiro Sakai

Extending hyperuniformity from classical to quantum fluctuations in electron systems yields a framework that identifies quantum phase transitions and reveals underlying gap structures through the quantum weight. We study long-wavelength fluctuations of many-body ground states through the charge-dens…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241113] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Extends hyperuniformity to quantum fluctuations in electron systems, using quantum weight to identify quantum phase transitions and gap structures.
motivation: To develop a framework for detecting quantum phase transitions and characterizing gap structures via long-wavelength charge fluctuations.
method: Analyzes long-wavelength fluctuations of many-body ground states through the charge-density structure factor and defines a quantum weight analogous to classical hyperuniformity.
result: Quantum hyperuniformity and quantum weight provide a unified description of quantum phase transitions and reveal underlying gap structures.
conclusion: The framework offers a new perspective on quantum phase transitions and electronic structure, but is primarily a condensed matter physics result with limited direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Vanishing Correlations In Stochastic And Bistochastic Controlled Circuits
authors: Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, and Tomaž Prosen

We study the dynamics of circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates. This type of dynamics arises from quantum circuits with random controlled gates, as well as in stochastic circuits and deterministic classical cellular automata. We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064139] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, with implications for quantum circuits and classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding correlation decay in controlled circuits is important for quantum information processing and statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates using mathematical proofs.
result: They show that such circuits exhibit vanishing correlations under certain conditions.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the behavior of quantum circuits with random controlled gates and classical stochastic processes.

title: Absorbing State Dynamics Of Stochastic Gradient Descent
authors: Guanming Zhang And Stefano Martiniani
abstract:
Author(s): Guanming Zhang and Stefano Martiniani

Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is a fundamental tool in stochastic optimization that is widely used in machine learning. Here, we study SGD through the lens of particle dynamics, introducing a framework that links its behavior to well-established models in nonequilibrium statistical physics. We i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062103] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper models stochastic gradient descent as a nonequilibrium absorbing state phase transition, linking machine learning optimization to statistical physics.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of SGD beyond convergence rates by drawing analogies to well-studied nonequilibrium processes.
method: The authors map SGD to a particle system with absorbing states and analyze its phase transition using scaling arguments and numerical simulations.
result: They identify a continuous absorbing state phase transition in SGD dynamics and characterize its critical exponents.
conclusion: SGD exhibits universal nonequilibrium critical behavior, providing a new perspective on optimization in machine learning.

title: Optimal Parametric Control Of Transport Across A Josephson Junction
authors: Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, and Ludwig Mathey

We present optimal control strategies for the dc transport across a Josephson junction. Specifically, we consider a junction in which the Josephson coupling is driven parametrically, with either a bichromatic or a trichromatic driving protocol, and optimize the prefactor of the [MATH] divergence of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023313] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Optimal parametric control of dc transport across a Josephson junction using bichromatic and trichromatic driving to enhance the supercurrent divergence.
motivation: To achieve high dc currents in Josephson junctions by optimizing parametric driving protocols, which is relevant for quantum devices and metrology.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to bichromatic and trichromatic driving of the Josephson coupling, solving for the prefactor of the 1/ω divergence.
result: They find that optimized multi-chromatic driving can significantly enhance the dc current compared to simple sinusoidal driving.
conclusion: Parametric control offers a practical route to boost transport in Josephson junctions, with potential applications in quantum circuits.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore the consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation in far-field cavities for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: Uses a specular ray-tracing algorithm to analyze thermal radiation in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Demonstrates violation of Kirchhoff's law and the existence of monochromatic thermal currents in the far-field regime.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities enable directional thermal transport, which could be useful for thermal management and energy conversion.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present a quantum information-inspired ansatz for the variational quantum eigensolver and demonstrate its efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems. Instead of adopting a heuristic approach, we start with an approximate multiqubit target state and utilize two quantum informa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023272] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum information-inspired ansatz for VQE to compute ground-state energies of atomic systems.
motivation: Improve VQE efficiency by using quantum information measures to construct ansatz instead of heuristic approaches.
method: Starts with an approximate multiqubit target state and uses quantum information tools to design a compact ansatz.
result: Demonstrates efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems with reduced circuit depth.
conclusion: The ansatz offers a systematic way to build efficient VQE circuits for quantum chemistry.

title: Quantum Finite-temperature Lanczos Method
authors: Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, And Giuseppe Carleo
abstract:
Author(s): Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, and Giuseppe Carleo

The computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in our understanding of quantum mechanics. We introduce the quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM), which extends the finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers by combining real-time qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023285] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum algorithm for computing thermal properties of many-body systems by combining real-time evolution with the finite-temperature Lanczos method.
motivation: Computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is challenging; classical methods like the finite-temperature Lanczos method are limited by system size.
method: The quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM) uses a quantum computer to perform real-time evolution and Lanczos iterations, enabling thermal state computation with polynomial resources.
result: The method is demonstrated on small systems and shows accuracy comparable to exact diagonalization, with potential for scaling to larger systems on near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: QFTLM offers a promising approach for quantum simulation of thermal states, but its practical advantage depends on future quantum hardware improvements.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and demonstrating convergence to diffusion processes in the continuum limit.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that allows for consistent treatment of observables across both jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of pathwise quantities in stochastic thermodynamics and related fields, but is primarily a mathematical tool rather than a direct contribution to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states of light, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide systematic optimization.
method: The authors define new control parameters beyond stellar rank and develop a theoretical framework to optimize state generation protocols.
result: The proposed parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The work offers a practical tool for designing scalable optical quantum sources, advancing photonic quantum computing.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a graphene-based device in a partially filled Landau level, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: Observed successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, achieving sensitivity that constrains the extraction of topological entropy.
conclusion: The measurements provide a thermodynamic signature of the underlying quantum phases, but the focus on condensed matter physics and topological entropy is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in information thermodynamics.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high encoding rate, and demonstrates constant-depth magic state injection.
result: Tricycle codes achieve high noise thresholds and reduce overhead for magic state generation compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward fault-tolerant universal quantum computation with reduced resource requirements.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying where quantum advantage may arise.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms and determining potential quantum speedups.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of computing matrix functions using quantum circuits, classifying regimes based on input parameters and error tolerance.
result: They delineate parameter regimes where quantum algorithms offer advantage over classical ones, and where classical algorithms remain optimal.
conclusion: The work provides a complexity-theoretic map for matrix functions, guiding future quantum algorithm design.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical simulation method for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum computing, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding and classically simulating quantum expectation landscapes is important for variational quantum algorithms, but full simulation is costly. The authors aim to reduce this cost by focusing on local patches.
method: They develop a classical surrogate model that approximates the expectation landscape in a small subregion, trained on data from a quantum computer. The method leverages the locality of the landscape.
result: The surrogate can efficiently predict expectation values in the patch with high accuracy, requiring fewer quantum evaluations than direct simulation.
conclusion: This approach enables efficient classical exploration of quantum landscapes, potentially aiding in the design and optimization of quantum circuits.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and understanding quantum advantage, especially for circuits dominated by Clifford gates.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling faster classical simulation.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach can simulate Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, reducing computational cost.
conclusion: Symmetry reductions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, which may aid in verifying quantum computations.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve super-Heisenberg scaling in parameter estimation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including the use of critical exponents and finite-size scaling, and discusses experimental platforms such as trapped ions and superconducting circuits.
result: It demonstrates that operating near a quantum critical point can yield quantum-enhanced sensitivity, but practical limitations such as critical slowing down and decoherence are also addressed.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a promising route to surpass standard quantum limits, but challenges remain in mitigating decoherence and achieving practical implementations.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors propose a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to achieve near-optimal gate complexity.
result: The framework yields near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum computing applications.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for products of Pauli operators and use it to simplify circuits in the sequential Pauli-based computation model.
result: The proposed relation enables significant reduction in the number of T gates required for certain quantum circuits.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count optimization, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to learn and extrapolate dynamics.
method: Fourier neural operators are trained on time-series data of observables to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and predict operator growth and dynamics beyond the training time window.
result: The method accurately reproduces Floquet Hamiltonians and captures long-time dynamics, including operator growth, for several driven quantum models.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method involves propagating errors through the circuit to the final measurement, allowing the simulation to be performed with reduced overhead. This is achieved by leveraging the structure of stabilizer circuits and error propagation rules.
result: The proposed technique significantly reduces the computational cost of simulating logical magic state preparation, enabling the study of larger protocols and error regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation protocols, which is important for the development of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes that are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, enabling single-shot correction.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements without extra overhead, preserving the code's performance characteristics.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on LDPC codes.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that such violations arise from violating underlying assumptions, and discusses how to design materials with extreme properties.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are widely assumed to be fundamental limits, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why and how to exploit this can lead to novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response, homogeneity) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent bound violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or hierarchical structures, and shows how these can be engineered to achieve extreme properties.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds by deliberately violating the assumptions behind those bounds, opening avenues for advanced materials with unprecedented properties.

title: Many-body Time Evolution From A Correlation-efficient Quantum Algorithm
authors: Michael Rose And David A. Mazziotti
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Rose and David A. Mazziotti

We introduce the correlation-efficient time-evolution (CETE) algorithm for simulating quantum many-body dynamics. CETE recasts each step of time evolution as a time-independent correlation problem: the ansatz begins from a mean-field single Slater determinant and is then correlated to capture the tr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060406] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A correlation-efficient quantum algorithm for simulating many-body time evolution using a mean-field ansatz with controlled correlations.
motivation: Simulating quantum many-body dynamics on classical computers is exponentially hard; quantum algorithms promise speedup but require efficient use of limited quantum resources.
method: The CETE algorithm reformulates each time step as a time-independent correlation problem, starting from a single Slater determinant and adding correlations via a parameterized ansatz.
result: The algorithm reduces the number of quantum operations (e.g., CNOT gates) compared to standard Trotter-based methods for certain systems, as demonstrated on small molecules.
conclusion: CETE offers a resource-efficient approach to quantum simulation, potentially enabling larger or longer-time simulations on near-term quantum devices.

title: Entanglement Dynamics For Atoms Near A Reflecting Boundary: Enhancement And Suppression By Environment-induced Interactions
authors: Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, And Jiawei Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, and Jiawei Hu

We investigate how environment-induced interactions influence the entanglement dynamics of two atoms held at fixed positions near a perfectly reflecting boundary. Within the framework of open quantum systems, we explicitly incorporate the environment-induced energy shifts, including both atom-bounda…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062437] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how environment-induced interactions affect entanglement dynamics of two atoms near a reflecting boundary.
motivation: Understanding entanglement dynamics in open quantum systems is important for quantum information processing, but the focus here is on a specific physical scenario rather than general information-theoretic results.
method: The authors use an open quantum systems framework, incorporating environment-induced energy shifts and solving master equations for two atoms near a boundary.
result: They find that environment-induced interactions can either enhance or suppress entanglement depending on interatomic distances and boundary conditions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into entanglement control via boundary effects, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core quantum information topics.

title: Magnon Diffusion Length And Longitudinal Spin Seebeck Effect In Vanadium Tetracyanoethylene $\mathrm{V}{[\mathrm{TCNE}]}_{x}$ $(x∼2)$
authors: Seth W. Kurfman, Denis R. Candido, Brandi Wooten, Yuanhua Zheng, Michael J. Newburger, Shuyu Cheng, Roland K. Kawakami, Joseph P. Heremans, Michael E. Flatté, And Ezekiel Johnston-Halperin
abstract:
Author(s): Seth W. Kurfman, Denis R. Candido, Brandi Wooten, Yuanhua Zheng, Michael J. Newburger, Shuyu Cheng, Roland K. Kawakami, Joseph P. Heremans, Michael E. Flatté, and Ezekiel Johnston-Halperin

The study of spin-thermal processes is limited by the small number of magnetic materials where these effects are easily distinguished and the limited regimes wherein the theory is tractable. This paper incorporates the temperature dependence of magnon nonconserving processes, demonstrating quantitative agreement with established data sets and leading to the prediction of a high‑efficiency regime defined by low‑magnetization, ultra‑low‑damping magnetic materials. This prediction is validated in the organic ferrimagnetic semiconductor V[TCNE]
[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220408] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon diffusion and the longitudinal spin Seebeck effect in the organic ferrimagnet V[TCNE]x, predicting a high-efficiency regime for spin-thermal effects.
motivation: To understand spin-thermal processes in magnetic materials and identify regimes where these effects are enhanced, given the limited number of materials where theory is tractable.
method: The authors incorporate temperature dependence of magnon nonconserving processes into a theoretical model and validate it against experimental data from V[TCNE]x, an organic ferrimagnetic semiconductor.
result: Quantitative agreement with established data sets is achieved, and a high-efficiency regime defined by low magnetization and ultra-low damping is predicted and validated in V[TCNE]x, showing spin-thermal effects comparable to yttrium iron garnet.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that organic ferrimagnets can exhibit strong spin-thermal effects, opening new avenues for spin caloritronics.

title: Breakdown Of Bosonic Thouless Pump Due To Interaction In A Quasiperiodic Lattice
authors: Suman Mondal, Emmanuel Gottlob, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner, And Ulrich Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Suman Mondal, Emmanuel Gottlob, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner, and Ulrich Schneider

Remarkably, even weak interactions cause of a breakdown of the quantized Thouless pump in a bosonic quasicrystal, despite its known robustness against disorder. Sharp jumps in the transport as a function of interaction strength are traced back to the closing of specific doublon channels. Most strikingly, repulsive doublons – two bosons occupying the same site – survive in the lowest band but dissociate in higher ones, draining energy from the driven system rather than heating it.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235131] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Interactions cause breakdown of quantized Thouless pumping in a bosonic quasicrystal, with sharp transport jumps linked to doublon channel closings.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of topological pumping against interactions and disorder is important for quantum transport and many-body physics.
method: Numerical simulations of bosons in a quasiperiodic lattice with interactions, analyzing doublon dynamics and transport.
result: Weak interactions break the quantized pump; repulsive doublons survive in the lowest band but dissociate in higher bands, draining energy without heating.
conclusion: Interactions can destroy topological pumping even when disorder does not, highlighting the fragility of such pumps in interacting systems.

title: Exact Steady States And Fragmentation-induced Relaxation In The No-passing Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
authors: Urei Miura
abstract:
Author(s): Urei Miura

We introduce a multispecies generalization of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with a “no-passing” constraint, forbidding overtaking, on a one-dimensional reflecting (closed) chain without particle reservoirs. This no-passing rule fragments the Hilbert space into an exponential number of disj…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064129] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a multispecies asymmetric simple exclusion process with a no-passing constraint, revealing Hilbert space fragmentation and exact steady states.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in constrained classical stochastic systems with many degrees of freedom, which may inform non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors introduce a no-passing rule in a multispecies ASEP on a closed chain, analyze the fragmentation of the Hilbert space, and derive exact steady states using matrix product ansatz or combinatorial methods.
result: The Hilbert space fragments into exponentially many disconnected sectors, each with its own steady state, leading to fragmentation-induced relaxation and non-ergodic behavior.
conclusion: The no-passing constraint fundamentally alters the relaxation dynamics, providing a classical analog of Hilbert space fragmentation seen in quantum systems.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-averaged displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using a generalized Langevin equation, focusing on scaling laws for anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of single particles in complex environments is important for biophysics and soft matter, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors reformulate the generalized Langevin equation in terms of velocity correlation functions and derive scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
result: They identify scaling laws for the displacement correlation function applicable to both normal and anomalous diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for analyzing single-particle tracking data, but it is purely classical and does not involve quantum effects or information-theoretic concepts.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting non-equilibrium steady states.
motivation: To understand the effect of resetting on underdamped systems, which are more realistic than overdamped approximations, and to explore how different resetting procedures affect the dynamics.
method: Analytical and numerical methods are used to solve the underdamped Langevin equation with Poissonian resetting, considering two protocols: full resetting of position and velocity to zero, and resetting position to zero while randomizing velocity according to Maxwell distribution.
result: The paper derives exact expressions for the probability density functions and moments of position and velocity, showing that the system reaches a non-equilibrium steady state with properties depending on the resetting protocol.
conclusion: Resetting in underdamped Brownian motion leads to rich non-equilibrium behavior, and the choice of resetting protocol significantly impacts the steady-state properties.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
authors: András Szabó And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases leading to out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases, accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To understand and control intertwined phases in driven quantum systems, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven collective excitations emerging from two distinct symmetry-broken phases, proposing a driven phase diagram.
result: The driven phase diagram hosts out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases that are tunable and accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for realizing and controlling intertwined phases in driven systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Optical Spin Pumping In Silicon
authors: Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, And Fabio Pezzoli
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, and Fabio Pezzoli

The optical generation of an out-of-equilibrium spin population is a keystone process for quantum technologies and spintronics alike. Although this is an established technique for studying direct band-gap semiconductors, it has been proven limited in materials that possess weak oscillator strengths …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023302] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical spin pumping in silicon, a key process for quantum technologies and spintronics.
motivation: Optical generation of spin polarization is established in direct band-gap semiconductors but limited in indirect band-gap materials like silicon; the authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors use optical spin pumping with circularly polarized light and measure spin polarization via Kerr rotation or similar techniques.
result: They achieve efficient optical spin pumping in silicon, demonstrating out-of-equilibrium spin populations.
conclusion: Optical spin pumping in silicon is feasible, enabling potential applications in quantum technologies and spintronics.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
authors: Peter Caradonna And Kenji Shimazoe
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, providing a method to certify entanglement without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting entanglement in high-energy photon pairs where standard polarization measurements are difficult.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry and derive that equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles (polarization symmetry) holds iff the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is a necessary and sufficient condition for the state to be a Bell state, enabling entanglement certification via Compton scattering.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for quantum information processing with high-energy photons, linking scattering phenomena to entanglement detection.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, specifically in periodically driven-dissipative systems.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional driven-dissipative chain using the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation and compute topological invariants.
result: They identify nontrivial Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics, including the emergence of exceptional points and directional amplification.
conclusion: Open Floquet systems can host topological phases without equilibrium counterparts, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes fermionic nonstabilizerness measures (magic) for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates using exact diagonalization or tensor network methods.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes of the binding-energy curve, indicating a connection between magic and bond formation.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary insight into molecular bonding, suggesting that quantum resources beyond entanglement play a role in chemical bonding.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana modes.
conclusion: The work offers tools to identify truly robust Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems, guiding experimental efforts toward non-Abelian braiding.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors use field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to derive a common mathematical structure for these systems.
result: They show how diverse models can be mapped to a single field theory, enabling systematic approximations and connections to quantum many-body physics.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful unifying tool for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with potential cross-fertilization between disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems for novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances in photoexcited Mott insulators.
result: Discusses mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to engineer nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators.

title: Quantum Non-Gaussianity Criterion Based On Photon Correlations ${g}^{(2)}$ And ${g}^{(3)}$
authors: Christoph Hotter, Clara Henke, Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen, Peter Lodahl, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Christoph Hotter, Clara Henke, Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen, Peter Lodahl, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

Quantum non-Gaussian states, which cannot be written as mixtures of Gaussian states, are necessary to achieve a quantum advantage in continuous variable systems. They represent an important benchmark for the realization of an advanced quantum light source, as they cannot be made by simple means such…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a criterion for quantum non-Gaussianity based on second- and third-order photon correlations.
motivation: Quantum non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but existing criteria are limited; a simple correlation-based criterion is needed.
method: Derives necessary conditions for mixtures of Gaussian states using g^(2) and g^(3) correlations, and tests them on simulated single-photon and two-photon states.
result: The criterion can certify quantum non-Gaussianity for states with up to two photons, including those with moderate loss and background noise.
conclusion: The proposed criterion provides a practical tool for characterizing quantum light sources, but is limited to low photon numbers and does not address entanglement or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities with improved efficiency.
motivation: Efficient spectral analysis of quantum systems is important but worst-case complexity is high; the paper aims to exploit structure in eigenvalue spectra.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to detect clusters and estimate multiplicities, likely based on Hamiltonian simulation and phase estimation.
result: The algorithm achieves better-than-worst-case complexity for certain spectral properties, enabling analysis of eigenvalue multiplicities.
conclusion: Quantum filtering can provide practical advantages for spectral analysis, though the contribution is algorithmic rather than foundational to quantum information theory.
