title: Theory Of Anomalous Landau-Zener Tunneling Induced By Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Wen-Yuan Wang And Hong-Juan Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Yuan Wang and Hong-Juan Meng

We develop a general theory of Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent, sign-reversible nonlinear coupling, distinguishing it fundamentally from conventional on-site nonlinearity. Through a combination of analytical and phase-space analysis, we show that beyond a c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062218] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of Landau-Zener tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent nonlinear coupling, revealing anomalous tunneling phenomena.
motivation: To understand how nonlinear coupling affects Landau-Zener tunneling, which is a fundamental process in quantum dynamics.
method: Combines analytical calculations and phase-space analysis to study the two-level system with nonlinear coupling.
result: Shows that beyond a critical coupling strength, the tunneling behavior deviates from the standard Landau-Zener formula, exhibiting anomalous features.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for nonlinear Landau-Zener tunneling, with implications for systems where nonlinear coupling is significant.

title: Equilibrium And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Dipolar Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, And Luca Salasnich
abstract:
Author(s): Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, and Luca Salasnich

An atomic Josephson junction realized with dipolar bosons in a double-well potential can be described by an extended Bose-Hubbard model in which dipolar interactions generate an effective on-site interaction and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling. Using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium and dynamical quantum phase transitions in dipolar atomic Josephson junctions using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
motivation: To understand the effects of dipolar interactions on quantum phase transitions in a bosonic Josephson junction.
method: The authors use an extended Bose-Hubbard model with dipolar interactions and analyze it via mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
result: They identify equilibrium quantum phase transitions and dynamical phase transitions, showing that dipolar interactions modify the phase diagram and induce novel dynamical behavior.
conclusion: Dipolar interactions significantly enrich the phase diagram and dynamics of atomic Josephson junctions, offering new insights into quantum phase transitions.

title: Application Of Quantum Annealing To Computation Of Molecular Properties
authors: Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present the results of our quantum annealing computations of the permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules. By applying an electric field as a perturbation and measuring the corresponding energy responses, the molecular electric dipole moments are obtained numerically through the fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062808] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum annealing to compute molecular electric dipole moments.
motivation: To demonstrate the application of quantum annealing for computing molecular properties, specifically electric dipole moments.
method: Quantum annealing is used to simulate molecular Hamiltonians; an electric field is applied as a perturbation and the energy response is measured to extract dipole moments via finite-difference method.
result: The computed dipole moments for several molecules are presented, showing agreement with known values.
conclusion: Quantum annealing can be a viable tool for computing molecular properties, though the approach is limited to small molecules and requires further validation.

title: Nonclassical Photocounting Statistics With A Single On-off Detector
authors: V. S. Kovtoniuk, M. Bohmann, And A. A. Semenov
abstract:
Author(s): V. S. Kovtoniuk, M. Bohmann, and A. A. Semenov

Any single on-off photocounter, which can only detect the presence or absence of photons without discriminating their number, is not capable of identifying the nonclassical nature of light. This limitation arises because any photocounting statistics obtained with such a detector can be easily reprod…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063726] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that a single on-off detector cannot certify nonclassical light, but two detectors can, using a witness based on photocounting statistics.
motivation: To determine whether simple on-off detectors can be used to identify nonclassical light, which is important for quantum optics and quantum information applications.
method: The authors analyze photocounting statistics from single and two on-off detectors, deriving a nonclassicality witness based on the covariance of click counts.
result: A single on-off detector cannot distinguish nonclassical from classical light, but two detectors can, as demonstrated with experimental data.
conclusion: Two on-off detectors are sufficient to certify nonclassical light, providing a practical tool for quantum optics experiments.

title: Optimally Driving Multiphoton Transitions In The Perturbative Single-mode Regime
authors: Frieder Lindel, Stefan Yoshi Buhmann, Andreas Buchleitner, And Edoardo G. Carnio
abstract:
Author(s): Frieder Lindel, Stefan Yoshi Buhmann, Andreas Buchleitner, and Edoardo G. Carnio

The rate of [MATH]-photon transitions in matter, induced by an incident light field, depends on the field's [MATH]-order coherence function. Consequently, the coherence properties of the light field may be shaped to increase the rate of multiphoton transitions. Here, we determine the optimal st…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063727] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes the coherence properties of light fields to enhance multiphoton transition rates in the perturbative single-mode regime.
motivation: Multiphoton transitions are important for spectroscopy and quantum control, and their rates depend on the coherence of the driving field. The authors aim to find the optimal field statistics to maximize these rates.
method: Using a perturbative approach, they derive the transition rate as a function of the field's nth-order coherence function and then optimize over all possible classical and quantum states of the field.
result: They find that for a given mean photon number, the optimal state is a Fock state for classical fields, but quantum states can achieve higher rates, with the optimal being a superposition of Fock states.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for designing light fields to maximize multiphoton transition rates, with potential applications in quantum optics and spectroscopy.

title: Ground State Energy And Phase Transitions Of The Long-range Xxz Chain Using Variational Quantum Eigensolver
authors: Mrinal Dev And Shraddha Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Dev and Shraddha Sharma

The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) has been widely used to find the ground state energy of different Hamiltonians with no analytical solutions that are classically difficult to compute. In our work, we use the VQE to identify the phase transition boundary for an infinite-order phase transitio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235132] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Uses VQE to study ground state energy and phase transitions of the long-range XXZ chain.
motivation: To demonstrate VQE as a tool for identifying phase transition boundaries in quantum spin chains with no analytical solutions.
method: Applies variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) on a quantum computer to compute ground state energies of the long-range XXZ chain and detect phase transitions.
result: Successfully identifies the infinite-order phase transition boundary using VQE.
conclusion: VQE can be effectively used to study phase transitions in quantum many-body systems, though the work is primarily a numerical demonstration.

title: Quasiperiodic Skin Criticality In An Exactly Solvable non-Hermitian Quasicrystal
authors: Zhangyuan Chen, Muhammad Idrees, Ying Yang, Xianqi Tong, And Xiaosen Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhangyuan Chen, Muhammad Idrees, Ying Yang, Xianqi Tong, and Xiaosen Yang

Critical states in quasiperiodic systems defy the conventional dichotomy between extended and localized states. In this work, we demonstrate that non-Hermiticity fundamentally reshapes this paradigm by giving rise to a class of quasiperiodic skin criticality. We introduce a non-Hermitian quasiperiod…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235423] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Hermitian quasiperiodic systems and discovers a new class of critical states called quasiperiodic skin criticality.
motivation: To understand how non-Hermiticity affects the nature of critical states in quasiperiodic systems, which are neither extended nor localized.
method: The authors introduce an exactly solvable non-Hermitian quasiperiodic model and analyze its spectral and wavefunction properties analytically and numerically.
result: They find that non-Hermiticity gives rise to quasiperiodic skin criticality, where all eigenstates are critical and exhibit skin effect.
conclusion: This work reveals a new paradigm of criticality in non-Hermitian quasicrystals, expanding the classification of quantum states.

title: Odd Toric Code In A Tilted Field: Higgs-confinement Multicriticality, Spontaneous Self-duality Symmetry Breaking, And Valence Bond Solids
authors: Umberto Borla, Ayush De, And Snir Gazit
abstract:
Author(s): Umberto Borla, Ayush De, and Snir Gazit

We investigate the quantum phase diagram of an “odd” variant of the two-dimensional Ising Fradkin-Shenker model, characterized by a uniform background of static [MATH] and [MATH] charges. Using large-scale tensor network and exact diagonalization methods, we determine the topology of the phase diagram, id…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum phase diagram of an odd toric code in a tilted field, focusing on Higgs-confinement multicriticality and valence bond solids.
motivation: To understand the interplay of topological order, confinement, and symmetry breaking in a lattice gauge theory with static charges.
method: Large-scale tensor network simulations and exact diagonalization are used to map out the phase diagram.
result: The phase diagram exhibits multicritical points and spontaneous self-duality symmetry breaking, leading to valence bond solid phases.
conclusion: The odd toric code model reveals rich physics beyond the standard Fradkin-Shenker model, with implications for quantum spin liquids and gauge theories.

title: Fractal-driven Universality In Quantum Transport Through Mesoscopic Devices
authors: F. M. Oliveira, Louis G. C. S. Sá, And J. G. G. S. Ramos
abstract:
Author(s): F. M. Oliveira, Louis G. C. S. Sá, and J. G. G. S. Ramos

We examine the impact of spatial fractality on universal quantum transport in mesoscopic systems featuring Sierpiński carpet scattering geometries. Transport calculations are performed using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework, allowing for a detailed…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064131] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of spatial fractality on universal quantum transport in mesoscopic systems using Sierpiński carpet geometries.
motivation: To understand how fractal scattering geometries influence quantum transport properties such as conductance fluctuations and shot noise.
method: Transport calculations are performed using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework.
result: The presence of fractality modifies universal transport signatures, leading to deviations from standard random matrix theory predictions.
conclusion: Fractal-driven universality emerges, suggesting that mesoscopic transport can be tuned by geometric fractality.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, and Alexandre Dauphin

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A comparative study of classical numerical methods for simulating the dynamics of the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
motivation: Understanding quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is challenging; this work benchmarks classical simulation methods to assess their performance and limitations.
method: The authors apply a suite of state-of-the-art numerical techniques (e.g., tensor networks, neural quantum states, exact diagonalization) to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model and compare their accuracy and computational cost.
result: The study provides a comprehensive comparison of the methods, highlighting regimes where each approach excels or fails.
conclusion: Classical numerics remain powerful for certain regimes, but quantum dynamics in 2D is still hard; the results guide choice of method for specific problems.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, focusing on topological phases that cannot exist in clean systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their analogy to quantum computation.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework by treating space and time on equal footing.
method: The review discusses discretized time evolution on lattice systems, brickwork quantum circuits, and the space-time duality mapping to simplify dynamics.
result: It provides a pedagogical overview of how space-time duality relates to exactly solvable models and quantum computation analogies.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding and computing quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

authors: Aindrila Sinha, K. P. Mithun, Shoubhik Mandal, P. S. Anil Kumar, D. V. S. Muthu, And A. K. Sood
abstract:

Polarization-resolved second-harmonic generation (SHG) is reported in highly doped [MATH], dual topological insulator, demonstrating the role of Rashba spin-split states (RSS) in driving a magnetization-induced nonlinear optical response. Steady-state measurements revea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224311] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.

method: Steady-state and time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements on highly doped Bi1Te1, with polarization resolution.
result: Observation of signatures of Rashba spin-split states in the SHG signal, indicating a magnetization-induced nonlinear response.
conclusion: The Rashba spin-split states significantly influence the nonlinear optical properties of dual topological insulators, which may be relevant for spintronic or optoelectronic applications.

title: $\mathrm{Li}A{\mathrm{Nd}}_{2}{({\mathrm{BO}}_{3})}_{3}$ $(A=\mathrm{Ba},\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}\mathrm{Sr})$: A Frustrated Spin-hexamer Lattice With Cluster-liquid-like State And Enhanced Magnetocaloric Effect
authors: Malik Ashtar, Xinyang Liu, Zhaotong Zhuang, Junsen Xiang, Zhaoming Tian, And Peijie Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Malik Ashtar, Xinyang Liu, Zhaotong Zhuang, Junsen Xiang, Zhaoming Tian, and Peijie Sun

The exploration of model systems exhibiting geometrical spin frustration remains a key avenue for uncovering emergent quantum phenomena. In this work, we report the synthesis and characterization of a different type of frustrated quantum magnets, $A{}_{2}{({}_{3})}_{…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224435] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of frustrated quantum magnets with a spin-hexamer lattice, exhibiting a cluster-liquid-like state and enhanced magnetocaloric effect.
motivation: To explore geometrical spin frustration in model systems for emergent quantum phenomena.
method: Synthesis and characterization of LiA Nd2(BO3)3 (A=Ba, Sr) compounds, including magnetic and thermodynamic measurements.
result: Observation of a cluster-liquid-like state and enhanced magnetocaloric effect in these frustrated spin-hexamer lattices.
conclusion: These materials provide a new platform for studying frustration and magnetocaloric effects, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multiple Correlation Lengths And Type-1.5 Superconductivity In $u(1)$ Superconductors Due To Hidden Competition Between Irreducible Representations Of Nonlocal Pairing
authors: Anton Talkachov, Paul Leask, And Egor Babaev
abstract:
Author(s): Anton Talkachov, Paul Leask, and Egor Babaev

The ratio of magnetic field penetration length [MATH] and superconducting coherence length [MATH] is a defining quantity that governs magnetic response and underpins the conventional type-I and type-II classification of superconductors. While multicomponent superconductors are known to exhibit multiple co…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224520] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies type-1.5 superconductivity in U(1) superconductors with nonlocal pairing, revealing multiple correlation lengths due to hidden competition between irreducible representations.
motivation: To understand the magnetic response and classification of superconductors beyond the conventional type-I/type-II dichotomy, specifically in multicomponent systems with nonlocal pairing.
method: The authors analyze a U(1) superconductor model with nonlocal pairing interactions, deriving the Ginzburg-Landau free energy and computing the penetration depth and coherence lengths from the resulting equations.
result: They find that hidden competition between different irreducible representations of the pairing leads to multiple correlation lengths, giving rise to type-1.5 superconductivity where vortices attract at long range but repel at short range.
conclusion: The work extends the classification of superconductors and highlights the role of nonlocal pairing and competing orders in producing exotic electromagnetic responses.

title: Second-quantized Approach To The Study Of Halperin State In Fractional Quantum Hall Effect
authors: Li Chen And Zhiping Yao

We validate this formula by proving that the second-quantized Halperin state, as recursively defined in this formula, …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235133] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a second-quantized recursion relation for the Halperin state in fractional quantum Hall effect, avoiding exact diagonalization.
motivation: To provide an efficient method to construct the Halperin state without solving the parent Hamiltonian exactly.
method: Derives a recursion relation for the second-quantized fermionic/bosonic Halperin state and validates it by proving the state satisfies the parent Hamiltonian.
result: The recursion relation is proven correct, enabling construction of the Halperin state for larger systems.
conclusion: The method offers a practical way to study Halperin states in fractional quantum Hall systems.

title: Skyrmion-resolved Topology In Chiral Topological Superconductors
authors: Bo-Wen Liu, Yu-Chen Zhuang, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Hao Wan, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Bo-Wen Liu, Yu-Chen Zhuang, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Hao Wan, and Qing-Feng Sun

Chiral topological superconductors (TSCs) are conventionally characterized by the bulk Chern number, which dictates the number of chiral Majorana modes at the boundary. However, this single invariant often obscures the rich momentum-space structure of the superconducting gap. In this work, we unveil…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235426] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a skyrmion-resolved topological invariant for chiral topological superconductors, revealing hidden momentum-space structure beyond the bulk Chern number.
motivation: The bulk Chern number alone obscures the rich momentum-space structure of the superconducting gap in chiral TSCs. The authors aim to provide a more refined topological characterization.
method: They define a skyrmion-resolved topological invariant based on the skyrmion number of the d-vector on the Fermi surface, and compute it for various chiral TSC models.
result: The skyrmion-resolved invariant reveals multiple topological transitions and predicts distinct Majorana edge mode signatures that are not captured by the Chern number.
conclusion: The skyrmion-resolved topology provides a more complete description of chiral TSCs and may have implications for Majorana-based quantum computing.

title: Anomalous Floquet Higher-order Topological Superconducting Phases Induced By Unconventional Pairing Symmetries
authors: Donghao Wang, Yongchun Tao, Jingguo Hu, And Fengliang Huang

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235427] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order topological superconductivity in Floquet-driven heterostructures with unconventional pairing symmetries.
motivation: To explore how periodic driving and unconventional pairing symmetries can induce novel topological superconducting phases beyond static systems.
method: The authors use Floquet theory and topological band theory to analyze a ferromagnet–2DEG–superconductor heterostructure with d-wave, p-wave, and s±-wave pairings.
result: They identify anomalous Floquet higher-order topological superconducting phases characterized by Majorana corner modes and nontrivial topological invariants.
conclusion: Periodic driving combined with unconventional pairing can stabilize higher-order topological superconductivity, offering a platform for Majorana modes.

title: Large Isolated Stripes On Short 18-leg $t\text{−}J$ Cylinders
authors: Tizian Blatz, Sebastian Paeckel, Ulrich Schollwöck, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:

Spin-charge stripes are among the most prominent competing orders in high-temperature superconductors. However, this phase is particularly challenging to study numerically due to finite-size effects. Here, we study the formation of long isolated stripes in the [MATH] model using…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of spin-charge stripes in the t-J model on 18-leg cylinders using DMRG.
motivation: Understanding stripe phases in high-temperature superconductors is important but challenging due to finite-size effects.
method: Density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations on short 18-leg t-J cylinders.
result: Observation of long isolated stripes and characterization of their properties.
conclusion: Provides insights into stripe formation but is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hyperfine Interaction Of Electrons And Holes With Nuclei Probed By Optical Orientation In Methylammonium Lead Iodide Perovskite Crystals
authors: Mladen Kotur, Nataliia E. Kopteva, Dmitri R. Yakovlev, Bekir Turedi, Maksym V. Kovalenko, And Manfred Bayer

motivation: Understanding hyperfine interactions in lead halide perovskites is important for spin-based applications, but the paper focuses on material characterization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Optical orientation with circularly polarized light, Hanle effect, and polarization recovery measurements in magnetic fields are used to probe spin dynamics and hyperfine coupling.
result: The experiments reveal hyperfine interaction strengths and spin relaxation times for electrons and holes in the perovskite crystals.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into spin properties of this material, but do not directly advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Non-Hermitian Higher-order Topological Insulators Enabled By Altermagnet Engineering
authors: Xiang Ji, Dengfeng Wang, Tong Zhou, And Xiaosen Yang

method: The authors theoretically show that proximity to an altermagnet can induce a transition from a first-order to a second-order topological insulator by gapping edge states.
result: They demonstrate the emergence of non-Hermitian higher-order topological phases enabled by altermagnet engineering.
conclusion: Altermagnet proximity provides an efficient route to engineer higher-order topological phases, but the work is focused on topological phases without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Giant And Robust Josephson Diode Effect In Multiband Topological Nanowires

tldr: The paper predicts a giant and robust Josephson diode effect in multiband topological Majorana nanowires.
motivation: To explore the Josephson diode effect in a realistic multiband nanowire setup, which may be relevant for experiments.
method: Theoretical analysis using a multiband model of quasi-one-dimensional topological Majorana nanowires, studying the interplay of Majorana bound states and Andreev bound states.
result: A giant and robust Josephson diode effect is predicted in the multiband regime.
conclusion: The multiband topological nanowires can host a strong Josephson diode effect, potentially useful for superconducting diode applications.

title: Triangular ${J}_{1}\text{−}{J}_{2}$ Heisenberg Antiferromagnet In A Magnetic Field
authors: T. Bader, S. Feng, S. Budaraju, F. Becca, J. Knolle, And F. Pollmann

tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of the triangular J1-J2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet in a magnetic field using spin-wave theory and DMRG.
motivation: The behavior of the triangular lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet in a magnetic field remains unsettled despite decades of study.
method: The authors use self-consistent nonlinear spin-wave theory, density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG), and exact diagonalization to map out the phase diagram.
result: They identify several magnetic phases and transitions as a function of magnetic field and frustration ratio.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive phase diagram for this paradigmatic model, resolving some long-standing questions.

title: Defect-mediated Melting Of Square-lattice Solids
authors: William Grampel And Daniel Podolsky
abstract:
Author(s): William Grampel and Daniel Podolsky

The melting of two-dimensional solids is driven by the proliferation of topological defects, a mechanism described by Kosterlitz-Thouless-Halperin-Nelson-Young (KTHNY) theory for isotropic lattices. Here, the authors extend this theory to square-lattice solids, where lattice anisotropy introduces an additional elastic constant and modifies the interactions between defects. The theory predicts two-step melting through an intermediate tetratic phase, but with key differences from the isotropic case: a modified bound on the translational exponent and nonuniversal Young’s modulus at the solid–tetratic transition.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214109] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Extends KTHNY theory of two-dimensional melting to square-lattice solids, predicting a two-step melting process via an intermediate tetratic phase.
motivation: Understanding melting in anisotropic lattices is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper focuses on classical defect-mediated phase transitions without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Theoretical extension of Kosterlitz-Thouless-Halperin-Nelson-Young theory to square lattices, incorporating anisotropic elasticity and defect interactions.
result: Predicts two-step melting with a modified translational exponent and nonuniversal Young's modulus at the solid–tetratic transition.
conclusion: The theory provides a framework for melting in square-lattice solids, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Giant Anomalous Hall Conductivity And Magnetostriction In Heavy-element Substituted Co-based All-$d$ Heusler Alloys

method: Systematic investigation of topological transport properties and magnetostriction in heavy-element substituted Co-based all-d Heusler alloys.

motivation: To develop room-temperature magnetic semiconductors for spintronics, overcoming the low Curie temperature of van der Waals magnets like CrI3.
method: First-principles calculations to investigate the effect of intercalation on magnetic properties and exchange interactions.
result: Intercalation enhances ferromagnetic coupling, raising the Curie temperature to near room temperature through synergistic exchange pathways.
conclusion: Intercalation is a promising strategy to achieve room-temperature ferromagnetism in 2D magnets for spintronic applications.

authors: Yizhuo Song, Jianting Dong, Jiahao Shentu, Chen Wang, Yurong Su, And Jia Zhang

method: The authors present a complete classification of spin-orbit torques in bulk collinear antiferromagnets using symmetry analysis and model the resulting spin dynamics.
result: A full classification of spin-orbit torques is provided, and the induced spin dynamics are characterized.
conclusion: This work advances the understanding of spin-orbit torques in antiferromagnets, which may enable future spintronic devices.

title: Gap Reopening As A Possible Signature Of Coupling Between Majorana Zero Modes In $\mathrm{Sn}\text{−}{(\mathrm{Bi},\mathrm{Sb})}_{2}{(\mathrm{Te},\mathrm{S})}_{3}$-based Josephson Trijunctions
authors: Duolin Wang, Xiang Zhang, Yunxiao Zhang, Heng Zhang, Fucong Fei, Xiang Wang, Bing Li, Xiaozhou Yang, Yukun Shi, Zhongmou Jia, Enna Zhuo, Yuyang Huang, Anqi Wang, Zenan Shi, Zhaozheng Lyu, Xiaohui Song, Peiling Li, Bingbing Tong, Ziwei Dou, Jie Shen, Guangtong Liu, Fanming Qu, Fengqi Song, And Li Lu

method: Fabrication of two adjacent Josephson trijunctions on the surface of a topological insulator and measurement of the minigap at the trijunction centers.
result: Observation of minigap reopening at both trijunction centers, whereas individual trijunctions would show gap closure.

title: Quantum Spin Liquid Ground State With The Evidence Of Roton-like Excitations At Elevated Temperatures In The Triangular-lattice Delafossite ${\mathrm{YbCuSe}}_{2}$
authors: K. Bhattacharya, Y. Tokiwa, And M. Majumder

Theory predicts that frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnets host roton-like excitations (RLEs) between two characteristic temperature scales. Here, using heat capacity and muon spin relaxation measurements on single-crystalline YbCuSe

title: Interplay Between Many-body Correlations, Strain, And Lattice Relaxation In Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Lorenzo Crippa, Gautam Rai, Dumitru Călugăru, Haoyu Hu, Jonah Herzog-Arbeitman, B. Andrei Bernevig, Roser Valentí, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Tim Wehling
abstract:

method: The authors develop a microscopic model incorporating electronic correlations, lattice strain, and structural relaxation.
result: The model accurately describes a broad range of spectral, response, and thermodynamic properties, matching multiple experiments.

title: Ferrimagnetic Blume-Emery-Griffiths Sawtooth Chain: Spin Ice And Quasiordering

authors: Ryosuke Kurihara, Atsuhiko Miyata, Koji Araki, Shusaku Imajo, Ruo Hibino, Atsushi Miyake, Sergei Zherlitsyn, Joachim Wosnitza, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Fumitoshi Iga, Masashi Tokunaga, And Yasuhiro H. Matsuda

method: High-field ultrasonic measurements of elastic constants in YbB12 single crystals, compared with transport and magnetocaloric oscillations.
result: No magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations were detected in the elastic constant, despite clear oscillations in transport and magnetocaloric data.
conclusion: The absence of elastic oscillations suggests a non-trivial electronic state in YbB12 that requires new theoretical understanding beyond conventional Fermi surface models.

title: Effect Of Spin-orbit Coupling On Spin And Orbital Ordering In ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{n+1}{\mathrm{Cr}}_{n}{\mathrm{O}}_{3n+1}$ ($n=1$, 2)
authors: Cristian Fanjul And A. A. Aligia
abstract:
Author(s): Cristian Fanjul and A. A. Aligia

We incorporate spin-orbit coupling (SOC) into effective Kugel-Khomskii models for the [MATH] and [MATH] members of the Ruddlesden-Popper series [MATH]. These models contain interacting spins 1 and pseudospins 1/2 at each site describing spin and orbit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235130] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-orbit coupling effects on spin and orbital ordering in Sr-based Ruddlesden-Popper compounds using effective Kugel-Khomskii models.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling with spin and orbital degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems.
method: Effective Kugel-Khomskii models are derived and solved to incorporate spin-orbit coupling for the n=1 and n=2 members of the Ruddlesden-Popper series.
result: The inclusion of spin-orbit coupling modifies the spin and orbital ordering patterns, leading to new magnetic phases.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling plays a crucial role in determining the ground state properties of these materials, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Paramagnetic Instability In A Tubular Nanowire With Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions
authors: R. A. Perrin And D. C. Marinescu
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Perrin and D. C. Marinescu

We describe a case of instability of the paramagnetic order in an electron gas confined in a thin tubular semiconductor nanowire with a Rashba spin-orbit interaction. This situation is realized when, for a critical value of the Rashba coupling constant [MATH], dependent only on the radius of the …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235310] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies paramagnetic instability in a tubular nanowire with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, a condensed matter physics topic without clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand magnetic order in low-dimensional electron systems with spin-orbit interactions.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model of an electron gas confined in a thin tubular nanowire with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, solving for critical coupling constants.
result: A critical value of the Rashba coupling constant is found that triggers paramagnetic instability, dependent only on the nanowire radius.
conclusion: The work provides insight into magnetic phase transitions in nanowires but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Persistent Current And Orbital Magnetization Along A Valley-contrasting Junction In Bilayer Graphene In A Magnetic Field
authors: K. Shizuya
abstract:
Author(s): K. Shizuya

In a magnetic field, bilayer graphene hosts an octet of pseudo-zero-mode (PZM) electron levels nearly degenerate in orbitals [MATH], valleys, and spins. They split in valleys by electrostatic gating. In gated bilayer graphene, in which the interlayer bias is set up to flip sign across a line, one…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235422] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies persistent current and orbital magnetization in a valley-contrasting junction in bilayer graphene under a magnetic field.
motivation: To understand the electronic properties of gated bilayer graphene with a sign-flipping interlayer bias, which creates a valley-contrasting junction.
method: Theoretical analysis using a low-energy continuum model for bilayer graphene in a magnetic field, solving for pseudo-zero-mode levels and computing persistent current and orbital magnetization.
result: The valley-contrasting junction leads to persistent currents and orbital magnetization that depend on the junction geometry and magnetic field.
conclusion: The findings reveal new magneto-electronic phenomena in bilayer graphene junctions relevant for valleytronics.

title: Quantum Phase Diagram Of The Bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg Model
authors: Elahe Samimi, Antonia Duft, Patrick Adelhardt, Kai Phillip Schmidt, And Saeed S. Jahromi
abstract:
Author(s): Elahe Samimi, Antonia Duft, Patrick Adelhardt, Kai Phillip Schmidt, and Saeed S. Jahromi

We study the ground-state phase diagram of the spin-[MATH] Kitaev-Heisenberg model on the bilayer honeycomb lattice with large-scale tensor-network calculations based on the infinite projected entangled pair state (iPEPS) technique with the simple-update scheme, as well as high-order series expansion…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245133] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ground-state phase diagram of the bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg model using tensor networks and series expansion, focusing on magnetic phases and quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To understand the interplay of Kitaev and Heisenberg interactions in a bilayer geometry, which may host exotic magnetic phases relevant to candidate materials.
method: Large-scale iPEPS tensor-network calculations with simple-update scheme and high-order series expansion are used to map out the phase diagram.
result: The phase diagram includes various magnetic orders such as ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and possibly spin-liquid phases, with phase boundaries determined.
conclusion: The bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg model exhibits a rich phase diagram, but the study is primarily a condensed matter physics investigation without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth gradients and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite defection being individually beneficial.
method: A game-theoretic model on a lattice where interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum of players' wealth, analyzed via simulations and possibly mean-field theory.
result: A discontinuous wealth-gradient transition drives cooperation.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can promote cooperation under certain conditions.

title: Universality And Ambiguity In Extremes Of Anomalous Diffusion
authors: Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Sean D. Lawley

Many biophysical processes begin when the fastest searcher finds a target out of many random searchers, which is called an extreme or fastest first passage time (fFPT). In some models (i) the fFPT vanishes logarithmically as the number of searchers grows and (ii) the fFPT can be faster for subdiffus…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of fastest first-passage times in anomalous diffusion processes, focusing on subdiffusion and superdiffusion.
motivation: Many biophysical processes depend on the fastest searcher among many; understanding how the extreme first-passage time scales with the number of searchers is important for modeling such processes.
method: The author analyzes mathematical models of anomalous diffusion (subdiffusion and superdiffusion) and derives asymptotic formulas for the fastest first-passage time as the number of searchers grows.
result: The fastest first-passage time vanishes logarithmically for some models but can be faster for subdiffusion; there is ambiguity in the extreme behavior depending on the model details.
conclusion: The scaling of extreme first-passage times is sensitive to the type of anomalous diffusion, with subdiffusion potentially yielding faster extremes than normal diffusion.

title: Resource And Population Dynamics In An Agent-environment Interaction Model
authors: Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, And Fernando Peruani
abstract:
Author(s): Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, and Fernando Peruani

In any ecosystem, the conditions of the environment and the characteristics of the species that inhabit it are entangled, coevolving in space and time. We introduce a model that couples active agents with a dynamic environment, interpreted as a nutrient source. Agents are persistent random walkers t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064406] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the coevolution of active agents and a dynamic nutrient environment, focusing on population dynamics and resource consumption.
motivation: To understand the entangled dynamics between species and their environment in ecosystems.
method: The authors introduce a model where agents are persistent random walkers that consume and deplete a diffusing nutrient field, with the environment regenerating over time.
result: The model exhibits complex spatiotemporal patterns and population cycles depending on agent motility, consumption rate, and regeneration timescales.
conclusion: The coupling between agent behavior and environment dynamics leads to emergent phenomena that cannot be captured by static environment models.

title: Complete Decomposition Of Anomalous Diffusion In Variable Speed Generalized Lévy Walks
authors: Abhijit Bera And Kevin E. Bassler
abstract:
Author(s): Abhijit Bera and Kevin E. Bassler

Variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) are a class of spatiotemporally coupled stochastic processes that unify a broad range of previously studied models within a single parametrized framework. Their dynamics consist of discrete random steps, or flights, during which the walker's speed varies…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, unifying several stochastic models.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind anomalous diffusion observed in many physical systems.
method: The authors analyze a class of spatiotemporally coupled stochastic processes called variable speed generalized Lévy walks and derive a decomposition of their diffusion behavior.
result: They achieve a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion into components, providing a unified framework for various previously studied models.
conclusion: The work offers a comprehensive theoretical understanding of anomalous diffusion in Lévy walks, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spectral Properties Of non-Hermitian Real Random Matrices With Long-range Correlations
authors: Ulysse Marquis
abstract:
Author(s): Ulysse Marquis

We investigate the spectral properties of non-Hermitian real random matrices whose entries exhibit long-range correlations decaying as [MATH]. We find a progressive breakdown of the circular law, controlled by the decrease of [MATH]. In all cases, the radial eigenvalue density decreases a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064126] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices with long-range correlations, focusing on deviations from the circular law.
motivation: To understand how long-range correlations in random matrix entries affect eigenvalue distributions, extending beyond standard short-range correlated ensembles.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of non-Hermitian real random matrices with power-law decaying correlations, deriving radial eigenvalue density and spectral observables.
result: A progressive breakdown of the circular law is observed as correlation range increases, with radial density decaying faster than the uniform disk.
conclusion: Long-range correlations significantly alter spectral properties, providing new insights into non-Hermitian random matrix theory.

title: Yielding In Dense Active Matter
authors: Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, And M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, and M. Lisa Manning

High-density granular active matter is a useful model for dense animal collectives and could be useful for designing reconfigurable materials that can flow or solidify on command. Recent work has demonstrated key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065410] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies yielding behavior in dense granular active matter as a model for animal collectives and reconfigurable materials.
motivation: To understand the mechanical response of dense active matter and its potential for designing materials that can flow or solidify on command.
method: The authors likely use simulations or theoretical models of high-density granular active matter to analyze yielding transitions.
result: Key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and passive systems are identified.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the physics of dense active matter, relevant to animal collectives and smart materials.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
Author(s): Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, and Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda

We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of surface ferromagnons in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator EuSn2As2 using antiferromagnetic resonance.
motivation: To study spin dynamics in the axion-insulating phase of a topological insulator, which is of interest for condensed matter physics but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Antiferromagnetic resonance measurements at 9.34 GHz were performed on EuSn2As2 single crystals below the Néel temperature.
result: Two types of resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and surface ferromagnon modes, indicating surface spin dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the magnetic properties of topological insulators but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Most Probable Path And Invariant Sets In Noise-induced Transition To Turbulence
authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, and Kenta Ishimoto

Turbulence transition often arises from a subcritical transition between bistable states characterized by invariant sets of deterministic dynamical systems, and such transitions can be triggered by system noise as rare events. In this study, we employ the Onsager-Machlup (OM) formulation of stochast…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023303] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise-induced transitions to turbulence in fluid dynamics using the Onsager-Machlup formalism.
motivation: Understanding the mechanism of turbulence transition from laminar to turbulent flow, which is a classic problem in fluid dynamics.
method: Applies the Onsager-Machlup path integral formulation to compute most probable transition paths and identify invariant sets in a stochastic dynamical system model of turbulence.
result: Identifies most probable paths and invariant sets that govern the noise-induced transition to turbulence.
conclusion: The Onsager-Machlup approach provides insight into rare event transitions in turbulence, but the work is purely classical fluid dynamics without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Macroscopic Localization And Collective Memory In Poisson Renewal Resetting
authors: Ohad Vilk
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Vilk

Stochastic renewal processes are ubiquitous across physics, biology, and the social sciences. Here, we show that continuous-time renewal dynamics can naturally produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure, with a macroscopic fraction of particles occupying a discrete state. For ensembles of continu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023305] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies macroscopic localization and collective memory in Poisson renewal resetting processes, a stochastic dynamics problem.
motivation: To understand how renewal processes can produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure with macroscopic occupation of a discrete state.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of continuous-time renewal dynamics with resetting.
result: Discovery of a macroscopic localization phenomenon and collective memory effects in the ensemble.
conclusion: Renewal resetting can lead to emergent collective behavior, relevant to statistical physics but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting and explaining dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear oscillators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
authors: M. Sumetsky
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies inelastic transparency in time-modulated resonant photonic circuits, focusing on frequency conversion and power amplification.
motivation: To understand and exploit time modulation in photonic circuits for frequency conversion and power amplification.
method: Theoretical analysis of a resonant photonic circuit with time-modulated parameters, using coupled-mode theory and scattering matrix formalism.
result: Complete inelastic transparency is achieved, where input light is fully converted to a different frequency with potential amplification.
conclusion: Time-modulated photonic circuits can enable efficient frequency conversion and amplification, with applications in classical and quantum photonics.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
authors: Tomonori Tanaka And Yoshihiro Gohda
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework combining spin-cluster expansion with noncollinear spin DFT to construct classical spin Hamiltonians from magnetic torques.
motivation: To efficiently derive accurate spin models for magnetic materials without requiring large DFT energy datasets.
method: Fits spin-cluster expansion models to magnetic torques computed from self-consistent noncollinear DFT, rather than to total energies.
result: The method yields accurate spin Hamiltonians with fewer DFT calculations compared to energy-based fitting.
conclusion: The torque-based approach is a practical and efficient way to construct spin models for complex magnetic systems.

title: Visualizing Phonon Edge States On Molybdenum Disulfide
authors: Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, And Jakob Schiøtz
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, and Jakob Schiøtz

Enhanced atomic vibrations have previously been observed near edges of two-dimensional materials with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM). Here this observation is accounted for by localized phonon edge modes by including correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022049] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses HR-TEM image simulations to show that enhanced atomic vibrations near edges of MoS2 are due to localized phonon edge modes.
motivation: Enhanced atomic vibrations observed near edges of 2D materials in HR-TEM were not well understood; the authors aimed to explain this phenomenon.
method: They included correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations to model the effect of phonon edge modes.
result: The simulations reproduced the enhanced vibrations, confirming that localized phonon edge modes are responsible.
conclusion: Phonon edge modes account for the observed enhanced atomic vibrations at edges of MoS2, providing insight into edge effects in 2D materials.

title: Emergent Self-attention From Astrocyte-gated Associative Memory Dynamics
authors: Arnau Vivet And Alex Arenas
abstract:
Author(s): Arnau Vivet and Alex Arenas

We introduce a Hopfield-type associative memory in which effective connectivity is multiplicatively modulated by astrocytic gains evolving under an entropy-regularized replicator equation. The coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics admit a Lyapunov function, ensuring global convergence. At fixed points, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023276] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A Hopfield-type associative memory model with astrocyte-gated multiplicative modulation and entropy-regularized replicator dynamics, showing global convergence and emergent self-attention.
motivation: To incorporate astrocytic modulation into neural network models to achieve more biologically plausible associative memory and attention mechanisms.
method: Coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics with a Lyapunov function and entropy-regularized replicator equation for astrocytic gains.
result: The model converges globally to fixed points and exhibits emergent self-attention-like behavior.
conclusion: Astrocyte-gated dynamics can produce attention-like effects in associative memory, suggesting a role for glial cells in cognitive functions.

title: Dynamical Learning In Deep Asymmetric Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, and Riccardo Zecchina

We investigate recurrent neural networks with asymmetric interactions and demonstrate that the inclusion of self-couplings or sparse excitatory intermodule connections leads to the emergence of a densely connected manifold of dynamically accessible stable configurations. This representation manifold…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023281] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical learning in asymmetric recurrent neural networks, focusing on the emergence of stable configuration manifolds.
motivation: To understand how asymmetric interactions and self-couplings in recurrent neural networks can lead to complex dynamical behavior and learning.
method: The authors analyze recurrent neural networks with asymmetric interactions, incorporating self-couplings or sparse excitatory intermodule connections, and study the resulting manifold of stable configurations.
result: They demonstrate that such networks can exhibit a densely connected manifold of dynamically accessible stable configurations, enabling learning and memory.
conclusion: Asymmetric recurrent neural networks with appropriate couplings can support rich dynamical learning, relevant to neuroscience and machine learning.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method for computing momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the huge system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network methodology that efficiently computes momentum-resolved spectral functions for noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral calculations in systems with millions of atoms, demonstrated on twisted trilayer graphene and other moiré systems.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a scalable approach to study electronic structure in complex moiré materials.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains shows they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: Develops a nonperturbative quantization approach for chiral solitons and analyzes their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and can be observed via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental detection methods.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories and uncovers emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand strongly interacting conformal field theories in three dimensions using a non-perturbative numerical approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the theory while preserving rotational symmetry, and perform numerical simulations.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the low-energy spectrum of the interacting fermionic CFT.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying 3D CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of such theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superstructures, which are of interest for manipulating information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures in EuAg4Sb2, combined with theoretical modeling to identify three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct magnetic phases are discovered, and a general framework for designing spin moiré superstructures is established.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for engineering materials that manipulate information through spin-based vortex lattices, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: To understand the stability of topological magnon gaps near the Curie point for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, linking to cryptographic protocol design.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptography.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using algorithmic and complexity-theoretic tools.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine learning models.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis using quantum Hall bilayer models and topological criticality concepts.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The findings offer a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which may host exotic magnetic order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe the magnetic phase transition and symmetry breaking.
result: The system exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the magnetic properties of kagome ice systems and the role of universality in frustrated magnets.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To find and characterize materials with flat bands that can host strongly correlated electron states, which are of interest for exotic quantum phases.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic band structure of layered transition-metal oxyhalides.
result: Intrinsic flat bands were observed that remain stable at room temperature, with orbital selectivity.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for studying strongly correlated electron physics at accessible temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: The authors perform magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, on twisted bilayer WSe2 devices under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: They observe a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstrate electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: The work establishes twisted bilayer WSe2 as a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall states and highlights the potential for electrical control of magnetic phases in moiré systems.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, focusing on density fluctuations and critical opalescence suppression.
motivation: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales, and understanding their critical behavior may reveal new physics at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and simulations to characterize the critical exponents and correlation functions of hyperuniform fluids near the liquid-gas critical point.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show anomalously low critical opalescence and enhanced susceptibility, with critical exponents differing from ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The unique critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids provides insights into the interplay between hyperuniformity and phase transitions.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling spin-based devices.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene with gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and spin-dependent electron optics.
conclusion: Ballistic spin valve in graphene is realized, offering a mechanism for coherent spin control.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: To understand the nature of long-lived hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems and their unique excitations.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation combined with resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe polaronic and phononic excitations in Pr0.67Ca0.33MnO3.
result: A long-lived hidden phase with distinct polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium is observed.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can induce metastable hidden phases with novel properties in manganites, relevant for understanding non-equilibrium states in correlated materials.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines robotic metamaterial experiments with theoretical modeling to study percolation of active forces.
result: Increasing activity can lead to vanishing macroscopic response when active units are too sparse to percolate.
conclusion: The phenomenon 'more is less' arises from percolation thresholds in active solids.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for topological data analysis with exponential speedup, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; the paper aims to demonstrate quantum advantage in this domain.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that computes persistence diagrams using quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques.
result: They prove an exponential speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of topological data analysis.
conclusion: The work suggests potential practical applications for quantum computing in data analysis, but it is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
