Despite heat flux's role in regulating energy conversion in collisionless plasmas, its properties and evolution in the magnetosheath downstream of the Earth's bow shock are scarcely explored. We use Magnetospheric Multiscale in situ measurements to quantify and characterize the electron heat flux in…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L063201] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron heat flux and whistler instability in Earth's magnetosheath using in situ spacecraft measurements.
motivation: Understanding heat flux regulation in collisionless plasmas is important for energy conversion processes in space plasmas.
method: The authors analyze Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission data to quantify electron heat flux and its relation to whistler waves.
result: They characterize the properties and evolution of electron heat flux and identify conditions for whistler instability.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into heat flux dynamics in the magnetosheath, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Vector Resonant Relaxation And Statistical Closure Theory. Ii. One-loop Closure
authors: Sofia Flores And Jean-Baptiste Fouvry
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Flores and Jean-Baptiste Fouvry

The dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole can be used as a test case for statistical closure schemes that allow the calculation of dynamical correlation functions in the fully nonlinear and nonperturbative regime. The authors develop an iterative scheme based on the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism, and find that it compares well with numerical simulations.

#AdvancingField #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064127] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a statistical closure scheme for stellar dynamics around a supermassive black hole using the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism.
motivation: To understand the nonlinear and nonperturbative dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole, which serves as a test case for statistical closure theories.
method: The authors apply the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism to derive an iterative closure scheme for computing dynamical correlation functions.
result: The iterative scheme compares well with numerical simulations, validating the approach.
conclusion: The proposed closure scheme is effective for modeling vector resonant relaxation in stellar systems.

title: Kinetic And Fluid Descriptions Of Jeans Instability In Kappa-distributed Suprathermal Astrophysical Plasmas
authors: Pooja Dalal And Ram Prasad Prajapati
abstract:
Author(s): Pooja Dalal and Ram Prasad Prajapati

The Jeans instability in an unmagnetized, collisionless self-gravitating plasma characterized by a kappa or Lorentzian velocity distribution is investigated in the framework of kinetic and fluid approaches. We have examined the role of suprathermality on the instability threshold wave number and gro…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065208] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Jeans instability in kappa-distributed suprathermal astrophysical plasmas using kinetic and fluid approaches.
motivation: To understand the effect of suprathermal particle distributions on gravitational instability in astrophysical plasmas.
method: Kinetic theory with kappa distribution and fluid equations are used to derive dispersion relations and instability criteria.
result: Suprathermality modifies the Jeans instability threshold wave number and growth rate compared to Maxwellian plasmas.
conclusion: Kappa-distributed plasmas exhibit altered stability properties, relevant for astrophysical contexts like interstellar medium.

title: Nonequilibrium Assembly Mechanisms Of Janus-polymer-grafted Carbon Nanotubes During Surface-initiated Polymerization-coupled Assembly
authors: Zhiyuan Cheng, Chun Liu, Yan Wang, And Hong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Cheng, Chun Liu, Yan Wang, and Hong Liu

Surface-initiated polymerization on anisotropic templates provides a useful framework for exploring polymerization-driven self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions. Here, we investigate surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly on idealized Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotube (CNT) tem…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065411] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium assembly of Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes during surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly.
motivation: To understand how polymerization-driven self-assembly on anisotropic templates can produce structured materials under nonequilibrium conditions.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to investigate the assembly mechanisms of Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes during surface-initiated polymerization.
result: They identify key parameters controlling the assembly process and predict conditions for forming desired nanostructures.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium assembly of polymer-grafted nanoparticles, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Plasma Flow Generation And Particle Acceleration From Expanding Magnetic Bubbles
authors: Yang Zhang, Brandon K. Russell, Geoffrey Pomraning, Lan Gao, Xiaocan Li, Adam Stanier, William Daughton, Chuanfei Dong, Liang Wang, Peiyun Shi, Kian Orr, And Hantao Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Zhang, Brandon K. Russell, Geoffrey Pomraning, Lan Gao, Xiaocan Li, Adam Stanier, William Daughton, Chuanfei Dong, Liang Wang, Peiyun Shi, Kian Orr, and Hantao Ji

Impulsive plasma dynamics in the laboratory are often driven by rising electric currents, yet their quantitative plasma response has not been well established. By means of fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations and laser-driven capacitor-coil experiments, we show that a rising current expels pla…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023317] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies plasma flow generation and particle acceleration from expanding magnetic bubbles using simulations and experiments.
motivation: To understand impulsive plasma dynamics driven by rising electric currents, which are relevant to astrophysical and laboratory plasmas.
method: Fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations and laser-driven capacitor-coil experiments.
result: A rising current expels plasma and generates expanding magnetic bubbles that accelerate particles.
conclusion: The findings provide quantitative insights into plasma dynamics and particle acceleration in such systems.

title: Revealing Charge Anisotropies In Metal Compounds Via High-purity X-ray Polarimetry
authors: Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, And Ralf Röhlsberger
abstract:
Author(s): Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, and Ralf Röhlsberger

Linear polarization analysis of hard x-rays is employed to probe electronic anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity. We use polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of [MATH] to determine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023297] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses high-purity X-ray polarimetry to probe charge anisotropies in metal compounds via nuclear forward scattering.
motivation: Understanding electronic anisotropies in metal complexes is important for materials science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors employ polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of 57Fe to measure linear polarization of hard X-rays.
result: The technique reveals charge anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity.
conclusion: High-purity X-ray polarimetry is a powerful tool for probing electronic structure, but the work is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Commissioning And Full Realization Of A Collinear Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy Setup At Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facility
authors: W. C. Mei et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): W. C. Mei et al.

A PLASEN (Precision LAser Spectroscopy for Exotic Nuclei) system, consisting of a compact radio-frequency quadrupole cooler buncher (RFQ-cb) and a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup, has now been fully commissioned with radioactive ion beams at the Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facilit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023286] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper describes the commissioning of a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup for exotic nuclei at a radioactive ion-beam facility.
motivation: To enable precision laser spectroscopy of short-lived isotopes for nuclear structure studies.
method: A collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy system combined with a radio-frequency quadrupole cooler buncher was built and tested with radioactive ion beams.
result: The setup was successfully commissioned, demonstrating its capability for high-resolution spectroscopy of exotic nuclei.
conclusion: The PLASEN system is now operational and ready for nuclear physics experiments.

title: Circular Dichroism In The Photoelectron Angular Distribution Of Achiral Molecules
authors: Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto de Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto De Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, and Peter Puschnig

Circular dichroism in the angular distribution (CDAD) is the effect that the angular intensity distribution of photoemitted electrons depends on the handedness of the incident circularly polarized light. The origin of CDAD can be manifold, including intrinsic properties of the system under study, su…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023275] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distributions from achiral molecules, a phenomenon in photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Understanding the origin of circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distributions (CDAD) from achiral molecules is important for interpreting photoemission experiments and for potential applications in molecular imaging.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements of photoelectron angular distributions with theoretical modeling using density functional theory and multiple scattering approaches to analyze CDAD from achiral molecules.
result: They show that CDAD can arise from the molecular environment and scattering effects even in the absence of molecular chirality, and they identify specific contributions from the substrate and molecular orientation.
conclusion: The work clarifies that CDAD is not exclusively a signature of chirality and provides a framework for disentangling intrinsic and extrinsic contributions in photoemission.

title: Excitation Of Confined Bulk Plasmons In Metallic Nanoparticles By Penetrating Electron Beams Within A Nonlocal Analytical Approach
authors: Mattin Urbieta, Eduardo Ogando, Alberto Rivacoba, Javier Aizpurua, And Nerea Zabala
abstract:
Author(s): Mattin Urbieta, Eduardo Ogando, Alberto Rivacoba, Javier Aizpurua, and Nerea Zabala

Using a linear hydrodynamic model, we theoretically investigate the interaction between penetrating electron beams and sub-5-nm metallic spherical nanoparticles. We derive an analytical expression of the electron energy loss probability that includes nonlocal effects in the response of the confined …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023279] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electron energy loss in metallic nanoparticles using a nonlocal hydrodynamic model, focusing on plasmon excitation.
motivation: To understand nonlocal effects in the optical response of sub-5-nm metallic nanoparticles when probed by penetrating electron beams.
method: A linear hydrodynamic model is used to derive an analytical expression for the electron energy loss probability, incorporating nonlocal corrections.
result: An analytical expression for the energy loss probability is obtained, showing how nonlocal effects modify the plasmonic response.
conclusion: Nonlocal effects are significant in small nanoparticles and must be accounted for in electron energy loss spectroscopy interpretations.

title: Membrane-associated Self-assembly For Cellular Decision-making
authors: Samuel L. Foley And Margaret E. Johnson
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel L. Foley and Margaret E. Johnson

Cellular decision-making based on information received from the external environment is frequently initiated by transmembrane receptors. These receptors are known to propagate such information by triggering a series of irreversible, energy-consuming reactions. While this active mechanism ensures swi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023280] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies membrane-associated self-assembly for cellular decision-making, a topic in biophysics and systems biology.
motivation: Understanding how cells make decisions based on external signals is crucial for biology and medicine.
method: The authors use computational modeling to simulate self-assembly processes on membranes triggered by receptor activation.
result: They show that self-assembly can act as a switch for cellular decisions, with timescales and thresholds tunable by molecular parameters.
conclusion: Membrane self-assembly provides a mechanism for robust and energy-efficient cellular decision-making.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and test the effects of heat treatment.
result: They find that silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, which has implications for coating design and postprocessing.
conclusion: The discovery informs strategies for coating deposition and postprocessing to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally tracks ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using ultrafast electron microscopy.
motivation: To directly observe and characterize ion diffusion in superionic conductors at ultrafast timescales, linking microscopic dynamics to macroscopic properties for better material design.
method: Ultrafast electron microscopy with pump-probe techniques to image and analyze ion motion in AgCrSe2 with high spatial and temporal resolution.
result: Direct visualization of ion diffusion pathways and dynamics, revealing the mechanism of superionic conduction.
conclusion: The study provides a direct experimental method to understand ion diffusion, aiding in the design of high-performance superionic conductors.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses and their relation to glass stability using inelastic x-ray scattering.
motivation: Understanding the connection between glass stability and vibrational properties is important for materials science but has no direct link to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use an improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique to measure low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: They find correlations between glass stability and the low-frequency vibrational spectrum, providing insights into the boson peak and related phenomena.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of glass physics but does not contribute to the user's research directions.

title: Subsurface Driven Size-Dependent Elasticity In Nanodiamond
authors: Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, And Chongxin Shan
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, and Chongxin Shan

Subsurface compliant regions in nanodiamond allow for an elastic response to strain, providing a method for engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021010] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond driven by subsurface compliant regions, focusing on mechanical properties of brittle materials.
motivation: Understanding and engineering the mechanical properties of diamond at the nanoscale is important for applications in nanomechanics and materials science.
method: The authors use experimental characterization and possibly simulations to investigate how subsurface structures affect the elastic response of nanodiamond particles of varying sizes.
result: They find that subsurface compliant regions enable an elastic response to strain, leading to size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond.
conclusion: The work provides a method for engineering mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond through subsurface design.

title: Boosting The Thermoelectric Performance Of $α$-MgAgSb Through Phase-Transition-Induced Self-Doping
authors: Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, And Huaizhou Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, and Huaizhou Zhao

A doping-free approach is able to boost thermoelectric performance, providing an attractive route for developing waste heat recovery technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021011] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a doping-free approach to enhance thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb via phase-transition-induced self-doping.
motivation: Thermoelectric materials can convert waste heat into electricity, but traditional doping methods have limitations. A doping-free route is attractive for developing efficient waste heat recovery technologies.
method: The authors induce a phase transition in α-MgAgSb to create self-doping, and characterize the resulting thermoelectric properties.
result: The phase-transition-induced self-doping significantly boosts the thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb.
conclusion: This doping-free approach offers a promising strategy for enhancing thermoelectric materials without conventional doping.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles, with applications in trapping, sorting, and pulling.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental demonstrations of optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques, emphasizing the role of spin and momentum densities.
result: It presents a comprehensive overview of the field, including recent advances in pulling forces and acoustofluidic sorting.
conclusion: The review highlights the rich physics and practical applications of radiation forces and torques, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and behavior.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of how pressure affects electronic structure, bonding, and phase transitions in these materials.
conclusion: High-pressure studies reveal complex behavior in transplutonium materials, but the field remains challenging due to radioactivity and electron correlation effects.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the nature of physics as a point of view.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics research, particularly in neural networks and associative memory.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture, not a technical research paper.
result: No new scientific results; instead offers a philosophical and historical perspective.
conclusion: Physics is a way of thinking that can lead to discoveries across disciplines.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by Geoffrey Hinton reviewing Boltzmann machines and their role in machine learning.
motivation: To present the historical development and significance of Boltzmann machines in the context of neural networks and artificial intelligence.
method: Lecture format summarizing key concepts and contributions of Boltzmann machines.
result: No new research results; retrospective overview.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines were a foundational step in deep learning, but the lecture does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; this review compares three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The paper reviews scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, highlighting cases where they are combined for a more complete defect picture.
result: The review demonstrates how these techniques can directly access atomic-scale disorder information in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes provides a comprehensive understanding of disorder, which is essential for optimizing semiconductor materials.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but many reactions are difficult to measure directly.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches for low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: Provides an overview of the state of the art in theory and new ideas for laboratory studies.
conclusion: The paper is a comprehensive review of nuclear astrophysics, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and self-consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating all data up to the end of 2022.
result: A new set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values supersede previous sets and serve as the internationally accepted reference for fundamental constants.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique using laser-induced ultrasound.
motivation: To provide an overview of optoacoustic imaging, its physics, and its applications in biological and clinical research.
method: Review of basic physics, instrumentation, and multimodal approaches combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Discusses the ability to achieve high-resolution imaging at depths of millimeters to centimeters using optical contrast.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable noninvasive imaging method with potential for biological and clinical insights.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of gravitational wave signals from the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can probe the first second after the Big Bang, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical models for gravitational wave production from cosmological phase transitions, topological defects, and other early-universe sources, along with detection strategies.
result: Summarizes potential gravitational wave signatures and experimental approaches for detecting stochastic backgrounds.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique window into the early universe, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys various software packages and their interoperability, focusing on the generation and use of maximally localized Wannier functions.
result: It describes the ecosystem's capabilities for computing band structures, topological invariants, and other properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling accurate and insightful materials simulations.

title: Standard Model Baryon Number Violation At Zero Temperature From Higgs Bubble Collisions
authors: Nabeen Bhusal, Simone Blasi, Martina Cataldi, Aleksandr Chatrchyan, Marco Gorghetto, And Géraldine Servant
abstract:
Author(s): Nabeen Bhusal, Simone Blasi, Martina Cataldi, Aleksandr Chatrchyan, Marco Gorghetto, and Géraldine Servant

We compute for the first time baryon number violation at zero temperature from Higgs bubble collisions and find that it can be of the same order as that from thermal sphalerons in the symmetric phase at electroweak temperatures. We study the dependence of the rate of Chern-Simons number transitions …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241803] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies baryon number violation from Higgs bubble collisions at zero temperature, a topic in high-energy physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To understand baryogenesis and the origin of matter-antimatter asymmetry, the authors investigate non-thermal baryon number violation mechanisms.
method: They compute Chern-Simons number transition rates during Higgs bubble collisions using numerical simulations and analytical estimates.
result: The rate of baryon number violation from bubble collisions can be comparable to thermal sphaleron rates at electroweak temperatures.
conclusion: Higgs bubble collisions provide a new source of baryon number violation that may be relevant for electroweak baryogenesis scenarios.

title: First Observation Of Deuteron-$\mathrm{Λ}$ Correlations At Rhic
authors: B. E. Aboona et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. E. Aboona et al. (STAR Collaboration)

Precise experimental information on hyperon-nucleon interactions is scarce but of paramount importance to our understanding of the inner structure of compact stars. In this Letter, we report the first experimental results of correlation functions between deuterons ([MATH]) and [MATH] hyperons in …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 242303] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: First experimental observation of deuteron-Λ correlations at RHIC, providing insights into hyperon-nucleon interactions relevant to compact star structure.
motivation: Hyperon-nucleon interactions are poorly understood but crucial for modeling the inner structure of compact stars like neutron stars.
method: The STAR Collaboration measured correlation functions between deuterons and Λ hyperons in high-energy heavy-ion collisions at RHIC.
result: First experimental results of deuteron-Λ correlations were obtained, revealing the interaction strength and scattering parameters.
conclusion: The data provide new constraints on hyperon-nucleon potentials, improving our understanding of dense nuclear matter.

title: Mean First Passage Times Of Higher-Dimensional Velocity Jump Processes
authors: Maria R. D’orsogna, Alan E. Lindsay, And Thomas Hillen
abstract:
Author(s): Maria R. D’Orsogna, Alan E. Lindsay, and Thomas Hillen

First passage phenomena arise across physics, biology, and finance when stochastic processes first reach a threshold, triggering downstream events. Examples include the irreversible exit from a domain, a biochemical reaction, and a financial selloff. While typical formulations involve diffusive moti…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 247102] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mean first passage times for velocity jump processes, which are stochastic models of movement with finite speed, applied to biological and physical systems.
motivation: First passage phenomena are important in many fields, but the paper focuses on velocity jump processes rather than diffusive motion, which is less common and requires new mathematical tools.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for mean first passage times in higher-dimensional velocity jump processes using renewal theory and partial differential equations.
result: They obtain explicit formulas for the mean first passage time in terms of model parameters and show how it depends on dimensionality and velocity distribution.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding first passage times in velocity jump processes, with potential applications in biology and physics.

title: Properties Of Heavy Cosmic Nuclei Phosphorus, Chlorine, Argon, Potassium, And Calcium: Results From The Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer
authors: A. Aceituno et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Aceituno et al. (AMS Collaboration)

We report the unique properties of cosmic phosphorus (P), chlorine (Cl), argon (Ar), potassium (K), and calcium (Ca) fluxes in the GV to TV rigidity range collected by the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS) on the International Space Station. With a total of one million events collected over 13.5 yea…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241002] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports measurements of cosmic ray fluxes for heavy nuclei (P, Cl, Ar, K, Ca) from the AMS experiment.
motivation: Understanding the properties of heavy cosmic nuclei provides insights into cosmic ray propagation and sources.
method: Data collected by the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer on the ISS over 13.5 years, with one million events, analyzed to extract rigidity spectra.
result: Unique fluxes of phosphorus, chlorine, argon, potassium, and calcium in the GV to TV rigidity range are presented.
conclusion: The results contribute to the understanding of cosmic ray composition and propagation, but are unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing Scalar-Neutrino And Scalar-Dark-Matter Interactions With PandaX-4T
authors: Tao Li et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Li et al. (PandaX Collaboration)

Scalar-mediated interactions may exist among neutrinos, dark matter particles, or between the two. Double [MATH]-decay experiments provide a powerful tool to probe such exotic interactions. Using [MATH] double [MATH]-decay data from PandaX-4T, we perform the first direct spectral search in th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241802] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses PandaX-4T double beta decay data to search for scalar-mediated interactions between neutrinos and dark matter.
motivation: To probe exotic scalar-mediated interactions among neutrinos and dark matter particles using direct detection experiments.
method: Spectral analysis of double beta decay data from the PandaX-4T experiment to constrain scalar coupling parameters.
result: First direct spectral search for scalar-neutrino and scalar-dark-matter interactions, setting new limits on coupling strengths.
conclusion: PandaX-4T data provide competitive constraints on scalar-mediated interactions, but no evidence for new physics was found.

title: Leading Effective Field Theory Corrections To The Kerr Metric At All Spins
authors: Pedro G. S. Fernandes
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro G. S. Fernandes

The leading corrections to general relativity can be parametrized by higher-derivative interactions in a low-energy effective field theory, in a way that is general and agnostic to the precise UV completion of gravity. Using numerical methods, we compute the leading-order corrections to the Kerr met…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241401] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes leading effective field theory corrections to the Kerr metric for all spins using numerical methods.
motivation: To parametrize and compute corrections to general relativity from higher-derivative interactions in a low-energy effective field theory, agnostic to UV completion.
method: Numerical methods are used to solve the modified field equations and compute corrections to the Kerr metric.
result: The leading-order corrections to the Kerr metric are obtained for all spins.
conclusion: The results provide a general parametrization of deviations from general relativity in black hole spacetimes.

title: First Experimental Limit On The Permanent Electric Dipole Moment Of The Deuteron
authors: A. Andres et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andres et al. (JEDI Collaboration)

Permanent electric dipole moments (EDMs) provide a sensitive probe of physics beyond the standard model and are directly linked to additional sources of [MATH] violation that could explain the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the Universe. EDM measurements of charged particles in storage rings rely on d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241801] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first experimental limit on the permanent electric dipole moment of the deuteron, probing CP-violating physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: Permanent electric dipole moments (EDMs) are sensitive probes of CP violation beyond the Standard Model, which could explain the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the Universe.
method: The JEDI Collaboration used a storage ring technique to measure the deuteron EDM by observing spin precession in an electric field.
result: They set a new upper limit on the deuteron EDM, constraining CP-violating parameters.
conclusion: The result provides the first experimental bound on the deuteron EDM, ruling out certain beyond-Standard-Model scenarios.

title: Observation Of The Radiative Decay ${D}_{s0}^{*}(2317{)}^{+}→{D}_{s}^{*+}γ$
authors: M. Abumusabh et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Abumusabh et al. (Belle and Belle II Collaboration)

An exotic meson’s photon-emitting decay opens a window into the particle’s long-debated structure.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241901] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Observation of the radiative decay of an exotic meson D_s0*(2317)+ to D_s*+ gamma.
motivation: To study the internal structure of the exotic meson D_s0*(2317)+ via its radiative decay.
method: Analysis of experimental data from Belle and Belle II collaborations.
result: First observation of the radiative decay D_s0*(2317)+ → D_s*+ γ.
conclusion: The decay provides insights into the nature of the exotic meson, supporting a molecular or tetraquark interpretation.

title: Laser-Plasma Based Seeded Free Electron Laser In The High-Gain Regime
authors: Marie Labat, Susanne Schöbel, Amin Ghaith, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Maxwell Laberge, Eléonore Roussel, Ulrich Schramm, Patrick Ufer, Marie-Emmanuelle Couprie, And Arie Irman
abstract:
Author(s): Marie Labat, Susanne Schöbel, Amin Ghaith, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Maxwell LaBerge, Eléonore Roussel, Ulrich Schramm, Patrick Ufer, Marie-Emmanuelle Couprie, and Arie Irman

The realization of compact laser-plasma accelerator (LPA) driven free electron lasers (FELs) has been attempted for nearly two decades, yet, difficult to overcome electron beam quality and stability issues prevented FEL lasing until recently. LPA based FEL is now demonstrated in both the self-amplif…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 245001] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a laser-plasma accelerator driven free electron laser in the high-gain regime, a milestone in compact FEL technology.
motivation: To realize compact free electron lasers driven by laser-plasma accelerators, overcoming long-standing beam quality and stability issues.
method: Experimental demonstration using a laser-plasma accelerator to produce high-quality electron beams and achieve FEL lasing in the high-gain regime.
result: Successful demonstration of LPA-based FEL lasing, marking a significant step towards compact FELs.
conclusion: Laser-plasma accelerator driven FELs are now feasible, paving the way for more compact and accessible X-ray sources.

title: Ablating Pellets For Areal Density Symmetry Control In Indirectly Driven Inertial Confinement Fusion Target Designs
authors: O. A. Hurricane, D. J. Strozzi, S. A. Maclaren, And C. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): O. A. Hurricane, D. J. Strozzi, S. A. Maclaren, and C. Weber

Asymmetry of the compressed fusion fuel configuration, as characterized by a variation in areal density, in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) implosions is a known performance limitation. While ignition has been achieved on the National Ignition Facility (NIF), implosion symmetry was not perfect, an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 245101] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method using ablating pellets to control areal density symmetry in inertial confinement fusion implosions.
motivation: Asymmetry in compressed fusion fuel limits performance in inertial confinement fusion; achieving ignition requires better symmetry control.
method: The authors propose and simulate the use of ablating pellets placed strategically to modify the radiation drive and improve areal density symmetry.
result: Simulations show that ablating pellets can reduce areal density variations, potentially improving implosion performance.
conclusion: Ablating pellets offer a viable technique for symmetry control in indirect-drive ICF, which may help achieve higher yields.

title: Tangential Forces Govern The Viscous-Inertial Transition In Dense Frictional Suspensions
authors: Sudarshan Konidena, Franco Tapia, Alireza Khodabakhshi, Élisabeth Guazzelli, Pascale Aussillous, And Bernhard Vowinckel
abstract:
Author(s): Sudarshan Konidena, Franco Tapia, Alireza Khodabakhshi, Élisabeth Guazzelli, Pascale Aussillous, and Bernhard Vowinckel

We present particle-resolved simulations of dense frictional suspensions undergoing the viscous-inertial transition using pressure-imposed rheology. By varying the fluid viscosity, shear rate, and granular pressure, we demonstrate that the transition occurs at a Stokes number of [MATH] (close to the v…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248201] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the viscous-inertial transition in dense frictional suspensions using particle-resolved simulations, focusing on tangential forces.
motivation: Understanding the transition from viscous to inertial regimes in dense suspensions is important for industrial and natural processes, but the role of tangential forces has been unclear.
method: Particle-resolved simulations with pressure-imposed rheology were performed, varying fluid viscosity, shear rate, and granular pressure to isolate the effect of tangential forces.
result: The transition occurs at a Stokes number near 1, and tangential forces are found to govern the transition, contrary to previous assumptions.
conclusion: Tangential forces are key to the viscous-inertial transition in dense frictional suspensions, providing a new mechanistic understanding.

title: Kinetic Theory Of Stimulated Brillouin Scattering With Velocity-dependent Collisional Relaxation
authors: Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Cooper K. Watson, Anatoly Svidzinsky, J. Gary Eden, And Marlan O. Scully
abstract:
Author(s): Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Cooper K. Watson, Anatoly Svidzinsky, J. Gary Eden, and Marlan O. Scully

In this work, we develop a kinetic theory of stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) based on a generalized Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) model incorporating a velocity-dependent collision frequency. Starting from the Boltzmann equation, we derive an analytic expression for the SBS gain coefficient that…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063523] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a kinetic theory of stimulated Brillouin scattering using a velocity-dependent collision model.
motivation: To improve the theoretical description of SBS in plasmas by incorporating more realistic collision dynamics.
method: Derives an analytic SBS gain coefficient from the Boltzmann equation with a generalized BGK collision term.
result: Obtains an expression for the SBS gain that accounts for velocity-dependent collisional relaxation.
conclusion: The model provides a more accurate prediction of SBS behavior in collisional plasmas.

title: Recoil Corrections To Muonic Hydrogen Hyperfine Splitting
authors: Andrzej Maroń, Mateusz Pańtak, And Krzysztof Pachucki
abstract:
Author(s): Andrzej Maroń, Mateusz Pańtak, and Krzysztof Pachucki

This work attempts to present a complete theory of the [MATH] hyperfine splitting, including all contributions above 1 ppm. Quantum electrodynamic and recoil corrections are calculated directly, while the proton structure correction is obtained with the help of the H hyperfine splitting. The …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062810] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates recoil corrections to muonic hydrogen hyperfine splitting using quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: To provide a complete theoretical prediction for muonic hydrogen hyperfine splitting, which is important for testing bound-state QED and determining fundamental constants.
method: The authors compute quantum electrodynamic and recoil corrections directly, and use experimental H hyperfine splitting to extract proton structure contributions.
result: They present a complete theory including all contributions above 1 ppm, achieving high precision.
conclusion: The calculated hyperfine splitting can be compared with future experimental measurements to test QED and proton structure models.

title: Step- And Terrace-resolved Crystal Truncation Rod Scattering From Vicinal Surfaces Under Coherent Heteroepitaxy
authors: Junlin Wu, Erqi Xu, Qihui Lin, Jiaqing Yue, Jiale Wang, Zihao Xu, And Guangxu Ju
abstract:
Author(s): Junlin Wu, Erqi Xu, Qihui Lin, Jiaqing Yue, Jiale Wang, Zihao Xu, and Guangxu Ju

We develop a general theory of crystal truncation rod (CTR) scattering from vicinal surfaces with a coherently strained heteroepitaxial film. The formalism incorporates film-induced interference fringes, full elastic lattice distortion, terrace ordering, surface reconstruction, and real-time growth …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235309] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a general theory of crystal truncation rod scattering from vicinal surfaces with coherently strained heteroepitaxial films.
motivation: To understand and model X-ray scattering from vicinal surfaces during heteroepitaxial growth, which is important for characterizing thin film structures.
method: Theoretical formalism incorporating film-induced interference fringes, elastic lattice distortion, terrace ordering, surface reconstruction, and real-time growth effects.
result: A general theory that can describe CTR scattering from vicinal surfaces under coherent heteroepitaxy.
conclusion: The theory provides a framework for analyzing X-ray scattering data from such surfaces, aiding in the study of thin film growth and structure.

title: Spatial Correlations In Susceptible-infected-susceptible Processes On Random Regular Graphs
authors: Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, and Michael Assaf

In network-based susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) models of infectious disease transmission, infection can only occur between directly connected individuals. This constraint naturally gives rise to spatial correlations between the states of neighboring nodes, as the infection status of connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064307] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatial correlations in SIS epidemic models on random regular graphs using pair approximation and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand how network structure and spatial correlations affect the spread of infectious diseases in SIS models.
method: The authors develop a pair approximation method that accounts for correlations between neighboring nodes and compare results with Monte Carlo simulations on random regular graphs.
result: They find that spatial correlations significantly impact the epidemic threshold and prevalence, and their pair approximation accurately captures these effects.
conclusion: Spatial correlations are crucial for accurate modeling of SIS dynamics on networks, and the proposed method improves upon mean-field approaches.

title: Plume Stretching In The Trapped Region Of A Reoriented Potential Mixer
authors: Roseanna M. Neupauer, James D. Meiss, And Tomás G. Dabove
abstract:
Author(s): Roseanna M. Neupauer, James D. Meiss, and Tomás G. Dabove

The reoriented potential mixer (RPM) can enhance mixing and reaction during in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater, in which a chemical or biological amendment is introduced into a contaminant plume to react with and degrade the contaminant. Each step of the RPM consists of dipole flow betw…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065108] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fluid mixing in a reoriented potential mixer for groundwater remediation, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Enhance in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater by improving mixing and reaction between introduced amendments and contaminant plumes.
method: Analyzes plume stretching in the trapped region of a reoriented potential mixer using dipole flow and numerical simulations.
result: Quantifies stretching dynamics and mixing efficiency in the trapped region.
conclusion: The reoriented potential mixer can improve mixing, but the paper is purely classical fluid dynamics.

title: Bifurcations And Multistability In Inducible Three-gene Toggle Switch Networks
authors: Rebecca J. Rousseau And Rob Phillips
abstract:
Author(s): Rebecca J. Rousseau and Rob Phillips

Control of transcription presides over a vast array of biological processes, including those mediated by gene regulatory circuits that exhibit multistability. Within these circuits, two- and three-gene network motifs are particularly critical to the repertoire of metabolic and developmental pathways…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064408] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bifurcations and multistability in a synthetic three-gene toggle switch network, a topic in systems biology.
motivation: Understanding multistability in gene regulatory circuits is important for biological processes and synthetic biology.
method: The authors use mathematical modeling and bifurcation analysis to explore the dynamics of a three-gene toggle switch network.
result: They identify conditions for multistability and characterize bifurcation scenarios in the network.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design principles of multistable gene circuits, relevant to synthetic biology.

title: Influence Of Visual Field Offset On Collective Behavior: An Exploration Using The Two-dimensional Vicsek Model
authors: Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, And Subhradeep Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, and Subhradeep Roy

This study investigates the influence of visual field offset—a restricted field of vision positioned at a fixed angle from an agent's heading direction—on collective behavior using the Vicsek model. This offset shapes an agent's ability to perceive and respond to neighbors, thereby impacting overall…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064409] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how visual field offset affects collective behavior in the Vicsek model, a classical model of self-propelled particles.
motivation: Understanding how limited and offset visual fields influence group coordination in biological systems.
method: Simulations of the two-dimensional Vicsek model with agents having a restricted visual field offset from their heading direction.
result: Visual field offset alters the onset of collective motion and the order parameter, with specific offset angles either enhancing or disrupting alignment.
conclusion: The offset angle is a critical parameter in collective behavior, with implications for biological and robotic swarms.

title: Topological Enhancement Of Protein Kinetic Stability
authors: João N. C. Especial And Patrícia F. N. Faísca
abstract:
Author(s): João N. C. Especial and Patrícia F. N. Faísca

Knotted proteins embed a physical (i.e., open) knot within their native structures. For decades, significant effort has been devoted to elucidating the functional role of knots in proteins, yet no consensus has been reached. Here, using extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple struc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062402] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how topological knots in proteins enhance kinetic stability using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand the functional role of knots in proteins, which remains debated despite decades of research.
method: Extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple structure-based model for knotted proteins.
result: Topological knots significantly increase the kinetic stability of proteins, slowing unfolding rates.
conclusion: Knots may serve a biological function by enhancing protein robustness against mechanical stress.

title: Flow Of Yield Stress Fluid In A Percolating Network
authors: Nathan Abitbol, Alex Hansen, Alberto Rosso, And Laurent Talon
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Abitbol, Alex Hansen, Alberto Rosso, and Laurent Talon

We study the flow of a Bingham yield stress fluid in a pore network model where the throats have radii drawn from a uniform distribution. We consider the case in which a fraction of the largest radii is blocked. The fluid can flow only through the percolating cluster that exists when the fraction is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065107] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the flow of a Bingham yield stress fluid in a percolating network, focusing on pore-scale physics.
motivation: Understanding how yield stress fluids flow through porous media is important for applications like enhanced oil recovery and groundwater remediation.
method: The authors use a pore network model with uniformly distributed throat radii, blocking a fraction of the largest radii, and simulate the flow of a Bingham fluid through the percolating cluster.
result: They find that the flow behavior depends on the fraction of blocked pores and the yield stress, with a critical threshold for flow onset.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the interplay between percolation and non-Newtonian fluid flow, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Performance Enhancement Of Direct-drive Shock-augmented Ignition Inertial Fusion Implosions Through Shock Timing Optimization
authors: M. Khan, K. Churnetski, D. E. M. Barlow, R. Betti, C. Freeman, K. Glize, J. Kunimune, A. Lees, R. Mancini, A. Nutter, R. W. Paddock, S. Regan, C. Stoeckl, W. Theobald, N. Woolsey, And R. H. H. Scott
abstract:
Author(s): M. Khan, K. Churnetski, D. E. M. Barlow, R. Betti, C. Freeman, K. Glize, J. Kunimune, A. Lees, R. Mancini, A. Nutter, R. W. Paddock, S. Regan, C. Stoeckl, W. Theobald, N. Woolsey, and R. H. H. Scott

Shock-augmented ignition (SAI) [R. H. H. Scott et al.,
tldr: This paper optimizes shock timing in inertial confinement fusion implosions to enhance performance of shock-augmented ignition.
motivation: Inertial confinement fusion requires improved resilience to instabilities and enhanced fuel compression for high energy gain.
method: The authors optimize shock timing in direct-drive shock-augmented ignition implosions through simulations and experiments.
result: Optimized shock timing leads to improved implosion performance and higher energy gain.
conclusion: Shock timing optimization is a viable route to enhance shock-augmented ignition in inertial fusion.

title: General Approach For Partitioning And Phase Separation In Macromolecular Coexisting Phases
authors: Vikki Anand Varma And Alberto Scacchi
abstract:
Author(s): Vikki Anand Varma and Alberto Scacchi

Partitioning of (bio)materials in polymeric mixtures is a key phenomenon both in cellular environments, as well as in industrial applications. In cells, macromolecules are distributed among distinct biomolecular phases. The coexistence of polymeric aqueous phases in multicomponent systems has been w…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065414] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies partitioning and phase separation in macromolecular coexisting phases, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: Understanding how biomaterials partition among distinct phases is important for cellular biology and industrial applications.
method: The authors develop a general theoretical approach, likely using statistical mechanics or field theory, to describe partitioning in polymeric mixtures.
result: The paper presents a framework for predicting phase behavior and partitioning coefficients in multicomponent polymer systems.
conclusion: The work provides insights into phase separation phenomena but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nanoparticle-mediated Interactions Governing Thermal Gelation Of Protein Dispersions With Tunable Properties
authors: Soumya, Sugam Kumar, Joachim Kohlbrecher, And Vinod K. Aswal
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya, Sugam Kumar, Joachim Kohlbrecher, and Vinod K. Aswal

Nanoparticle-protein dispersions constitute complex soft materials in which competing attractive and repulsive interactions can strongly influence their phase behavior, including gelation. In this work, we demonstrate a strategy to utilize interaction between anionic silica nanoparticles and anionic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065415] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies gelation in nanoparticle-protein dispersions, focusing on tunable interactions and phase behavior.
motivation: Understanding and controlling gelation in soft materials is important for applications in food, cosmetics, and biomaterials.
method: Small-angle neutron scattering and rheology are used to probe structure and dynamics of silica nanoparticle and protein dispersions.
result: The gelation temperature and mechanical properties can be tuned by varying nanoparticle concentration and protein type.
conclusion: Nanoparticle-mediated interactions provide a route to design protein gels with desired properties.

title: Regulating Droplet-surface Contact Time Via A Predeposited Microparticle
authors: Chao-Sheng Li, Shun-Jie Wu, Rong-Rong Cai, And Li-Zhi Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chao-Sheng Li, Shun-Jie Wu, Rong-Rong Cai, and Li-Zhi Zhang

Regulating droplet-surface contact time is a core demand for optimizing performance in inkjet printing, spray cooling, agricultural spraying, and other industrial fields. Conventional strategies relying on surface microstructure modification suffer from high fabrication costs and compromised surface…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065104] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies droplet-surface contact time regulation using a predeposited microparticle, relevant to fluid dynamics and industrial applications.
motivation: Controlling droplet-surface contact time is important for inkjet printing, spray cooling, and agriculture, but conventional surface microstructure methods are costly and compromise surface properties.
method: The authors propose using a predeposited microparticle on the surface to modify droplet dynamics and measure contact time experimentally and via simulations.
result: The microparticle reduces contact time significantly compared to flat surfaces, with optimal particle size and position identified.
conclusion: This approach offers a simple, low-cost alternative to microstructure-based methods for regulating droplet contact time.

title: Amplitude Variation In Spanwise Wall Oscillations: Effects On Drag Reduction And Heat Transfer In Compressible Turbulent Channel Flow
authors: Fangliang Xu, Wei Liu, And Peng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Fangliang Xu, Wei Liu, and Peng Zhang

Spanwise Wall Oscillation is a promising active flow control technique for turbulent skin-friction drag reduction (DR). While the effectiveness of the method in incompressible flows is well documented, its performance in compressible regimes, and the underlying physical mechanisms, particularly thos…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065105] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies drag reduction and heat transfer in compressible turbulent channel flow using spanwise wall oscillations, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the effectiveness of spanwise wall oscillation for drag reduction in compressible flows, which is less studied than in incompressible flows.
method: Direct numerical simulations of compressible turbulent channel flow with spanwise wall oscillations, analyzing the effects on skin-friction drag and heat transfer.
result: The amplitude of wall oscillation significantly affects drag reduction and heat transfer, with optimal amplitudes identified for compressible regimes.
conclusion: Spanwise wall oscillation remains effective for drag reduction in compressible flows, but the underlying mechanisms differ from incompressible cases due to compressibility effects.

method: The authors analyze the wave equation in two dimensions, focusing on the persistent wake tail that violates Huygens' principle, and examine its impact on refocusing.

motivation: Understanding bubble dynamics near inclusions is important for applications like ultrasound contrast agents and targeted drug delivery.

result: The model predicts resonance frequencies and damping rates as functions of inclusion size, material properties, and bubble-inclusion distance.
conclusion: The analytical model provides insights into bubble-inclusion interactions, which can guide experimental design in acoustics.

result: Facilitating compression yields effects on displacement patterns.

title: Leidenfrost Hydrogels: Elastic Surface-wave Instability And Sustained Bouncing
authors: Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, And James E. Sprittles

This work investigates the oscillatory dynamics and subsequent sustained bouncing behavior of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a phenomenon that has received little theoretical attention to date. Building on previous approaches toward drop impacts and Leidenfrost drops, a computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022052] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the oscillatory dynamics and sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a fluid dynamics phenomenon.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing in Leidenfrost hydrogels, which has received little theoretical attention.
method: A computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics of Leidenfrost hydrogels.
result: The model reveals an elastic surface-wave instability that sustains bouncing.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into a novel bouncing regime for soft materials on hot surfaces.

title: Tracking Phase Synchronization Between Flagella In The Time-frequency Domain Resolves Photophobic Response

This work aims to study the resynchronization of CR flagella after a high light intensity stimulus, known as photoshock. The synchronization is estimated thanks to a qu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023294] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flagellar synchronization in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii using time-frequency analysis to understand photophobic response.

title: When Surface Dynamics Fakes Symmetry: Oxygen On Rh(100) Revisited
authors: Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, And M. Alexander Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, and M. Alexander Schneider

Heating a long-range ordered adsorbate phase beyond its stability temperature does not necessarily result in a disordered phase; it can also break up into heavily fluctuating ordered domains. Temporal and/or spatial averaging over these fluctuations may give the impression of both a wrong periodicit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023296] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oxygen adsorption on Rh(100) surface, revealing that fluctuating ordered domains can mimic a wrong surface symmetry under thermal averaging.
motivation: To understand the behavior of adsorbate phases beyond their stability temperature and the misinterpretation of surface symmetry due to temporal/spatial averaging.
method: Surface X-ray diffraction and scanning tunneling microscopy combined with simulations to analyze the structure and dynamics of the oxygen overlayer.
result: The observed apparent (2×2) periodicity is actually due to fluctuating (2×1) domains, not a true (2×2) phase.
conclusion: Care must be taken in interpreting surface symmetries from diffraction patterns when domain fluctuations are present.

title: Controlled Interference Of Laser-induced Shock Waves In Microdroplet Jetting

We report the formation of high-velocity microjets driven by the interference of two laser-induced shock waves in a tin microdroplet. A first 0.4-ns laser pulse launches a shock wave into the droplet (diameter [MATH], 50, and [MATH]). Due to the droplet's s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023287] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies laser-induced shock waves in tin microdroplets to produce high-velocity microjets, with applications in extreme ultraviolet lithography.
motivation: To understand and control the formation of microjets from laser-driven droplets for industrial applications such as EUV light sources.
method: Two laser pulses create interfering shock waves in a tin droplet; high-speed imaging and simulations characterize the jet dynamics.
result: Controlled interference of shock waves enables tuning of jet velocity and direction.
conclusion: The technique offers a method to produce directed, high-speed microjets with potential for lithography.

title: Sea-surface Retention Effect Shapes Ocean Microplastic Fibers
authors: Andrea Mazzino And Giuseppe Suaria
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Mazzino and Giuseppe Suaria

Microfibers contaminate the global ocean, but their impact depends on length-dependent residence at the air-sea interface. In the submillimeter range, the sea surface exhibits a surface-enrichment signature: The long-to-short fiber ratio is higher at the interface than a few meters below (about 5 m)…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023283] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the length-dependent retention of microplastic fibers at the sea surface, finding that longer fibers are enriched at the air-sea interface compared to subsurface waters.
motivation: Microplastic fibers are a major pollutant in the ocean, but their vertical distribution and residence time at the sea surface are poorly understood, which affects estimates of their environmental impact.
method: The authors combine field measurements of fiber length distributions at the sea surface and at 5 m depth with a theoretical model of turbulent mixing and buoyancy to explain the observed surface enrichment of longer fibers.
result: The sea surface retains longer microfibers preferentially, leading to a higher long-to-short fiber ratio at the interface than a few meters below.
conclusion: The surface retention effect must be accounted for when assessing the transport, degradation, and ecological impact of microplastic fibers in the ocean.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically demonstrate super-resonance in a system of coupled resonators, showing that a broadband out-of-phase response can be maintained beyond the usual bandwidth.
result: Super-resonance achieves a broadband response that significantly exceeds the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling effective flow stabilization.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems with potential applications in flow control and other fields requiring broadband response.
